0168 | 
0169 |     def _collate_fn(self, batch, embedding_store, device):
0170 |         """
0171 |         Convert batch of examples to tensors
0172 |         """
0173 |         ctxs, docs_a, docs_b, labels = [], [], [], []
0174 |         
0175 |         for item in batch:
0176 |             # Get embeddings
0177 |             ctx_emb = torch.tensor(embedding_store.get_or_create(item["context"])).to(device)
0178 |             a_emb = torch.tensor(embedding_store.get_or_create(item["output_a"])).to(device)
0179 |             b_emb = torch.tensor(embedding_store.get_or_create(item["output_b"])).to(device)
0180 |             
0181 |             # Contrastive loss labels
0182 |             preferred = "a" if item["value_a"] > item["value_b"] else "b"
0183 |             labels.append(1.0 if preferred == "a" else 0.0)
0184 |             
0185 |             ctxs.append(ctx_emb)
0186 |             docs_a.append(a_emb)
0187 |             docs_b.append(b_emb)
0188 |         
0189 |         # Stack tensors
0190 |         ctx_tensor = torch.stack(ctxs)
0191 |         doc_a_tensor = torch.stack(docs_a)
0192 |         doc_b_tensor = torch.stack(docs_b)
0193 |         label_tensor = torch.tensor(labels, dtype=torch.float32).to(device)
0194 |         
0195 |         return ctx_tensor, doc_a_tensor, doc_b_tensor, label_tensor
0196 | 
0197 |     def contrastive_loss(self, energy_a, energy_b, label):
0198 |         """
0199 |         Contrastive loss for refinement training
0200 |         """
0201 |         # Label: 1 if a is better than b, 0 otherwise
0202 |         margin = self.cfg.get("loss_margin", 1.0)
0203 |         distances = torch.abs(energy_a - energy_b)
0204 |         
0205 |         # Calculate loss
0206 |         if label == 1:
0207 |             return distances  # We want energy_a < energy_b → smaller distance is good
0208 |         else:
0209 |             return torch.relu(margin - distances)  # Push apart if margin not met
0210 | 
0211 |     def train_refinement_model(self, dimension: str, dataloader: DataLoader):
0212 |         """
0213 |         Train EBT model for a single dimension
0214 |         """
0215 |         # Initialize fresh model for this dimension
0216 |         model = self._initialize_dimension_model(dimension)
0217 |         model.to(self.device)
0218 |         model.train()
0219 |         
0220 |         optimizer = optim.Adam(model.parameters(), lr=self.lr)
0221 | 
0222 |         
0223 |         for epoch in range(self.epochs):
0224 |             epoch_loss = 0.0
0225 |             
0226 |             for ctx, doc_a, doc_b, labels in dataloader:
0227 |                 optimizer.zero_grad()
0228 |                 
0229 |                 # Forward pass
0230 |                 energy_a = model(ctx, doc_a)
0231 |                 energy_b = model(ctx, doc_b)
0232 |                 
0233 |                 # Calculate loss
0234 |                 loss = self.contrastive_loss(energy_a, energy_b, labels).mean()
0235 |                 loss.backward()
0236 |                 optimizer.step()
0237 |                 
0238 |                 epoch_loss += loss.item()
0239 |             
0240 |             avg_epoch_loss = epoch_loss / len(dataloader)
0241 |             self.logger.log("EBTRefinementEpoch", {
0242 |                 "dimension": dimension,
0243 |                 "epoch": epoch + 1,
0244 |                 "loss": avg_epoch_loss
0245 |             })
0246 |             
0247 |             # Periodic model saving
0248 |             if (epoch + 1) % self.save_interval == 0:
0249 |                 self._save_model(model, dimension, f"v{epoch + 1}")
0250 |         
0251 |         # Final save
0252 |         final_path = self._save_model(model, dimension, "latest")
0253 |         self.logger.log("EBTRefinementTrainingComplete", {
0254 |             "dimension": dimension,
0255 |             "final_loss": avg_epoch_loss,
0256 |             "model_path": final_path
0257 |         })
0258 |         return model
0259 | 
0260 |     def _initialize_dimension_model(self, dimension: str) -> EBTModel:
0261 |         """Initialize a fresh EBT model for a dimension"""
0262 |         model_path = get_model_path(
0263 |             self.model_path,
0264 |             self.model_type,
0265 |             self.target_type,
0266 |             dimension,
0267 |             self.model_version,
0268 |             self.embedding_type
0269 |         )
0270 |         os.makedirs(model_path, exist_ok=True)
0271 |         
0272 |         return EBTModel().to(self.device)
0273 | 
0274 |     def _save_model(self, model, dimension: str, version: str = "latest") -> str:
0275 |         """Save model and metadata"""
0276 |         model_path = get_model_path(
0277 |             self.model_path,
0278 |             self.model_type,
0279 |             self.target_type,
0280 |             dimension,
0281 |             version
0282 |         )
0283 |         
0284 |         # Save model weights
0285 |         torch.save(model.state_dict(), os.path.join(model_path, f"{dimension}.pt"))
0286 |         
0287 |         # Save normalization metadata
0288 |         meta_path = os.path.join(model_path, f"{dimension}.meta.json")
0289 |         meta = {
0290 |             "min_value": self.ebt_meta.get(dimension, {}).get("min", 40),
0291 |             "max_value": self.ebt_meta.get(dimension, {}).get("max", 100),
0292 |             "train_min_value": self._get_train_min_value(dimension),
0293 |             "train_max_value": self._get_train_max_value(dimension),
0294 |             "training_date": datetime.now().isoformat(),
0295 |             "version": version
0296 |         }
0297 |         save_json(meta, meta_path)
0298 |         
0299 |         return model_path
0300 | 
0301 |     def _get_train_min_value(self, dimension: str):
0302 |         """Get training minimum score for normalization"""
0303 |         query = f"""
0304 |         SELECT MIN(score) FROM scoring_events
0305 |         WHERE dimension='{dimension}' AND source IN ('ebt', 'llm')
0306 |         """
0307 |         result = self.memory.db.execute(query).fetchone()
0308 |         return result[0] if result else 40
0309 | 
0310 |     def srft_loss(self, energy_orig, energy_ref, llm_score=None, orig_score=None, ref_score=None, entropy=None):
0311 |         """
0312 |         SRFT-style loss combining:
0313 |         - Supervised Fine-Tuning (match LLM score or gold refined score)
0314 |         - Reinforcement-style reward (improve MRQ score or reduce energy)
0315 |         """
0316 |         losses = []
0317 | 
0318 |         # 1. SFT: encourage refined to match or beat LLM score
0319 |         if llm_score is not None:
0320 |             target = torch.tensor(llm_score).to(self.device)
0321 |             losses.append(torch.nn.functional.mse_loss(energy_ref, target))
0322 | 
0323 |         # 2. RL-style reward: reward if refined energy < original
0324 |         if energy_orig is not None:
0325 |             margin = self.cfg.get("rl_margin", 0.05)
0326 |             diff = energy_orig - energy_ref
0327 |             rl_loss = -torch.relu(diff - margin)  # reward if improvement
0328 |             losses.append(rl_loss.mean())
0329 | 
0330 |         # 3. Entropy-aware weighting (optional)
0331 |         if entropy is not None:
0332 |             weight = 1.0 / (1.0 + entropy)
0333 |             total = sum(losses)
0334 |             return weight * total
0335 | 
0336 |         return sum(losses)
0337 | 
0338 | 
0339 |     def _get_train_max_value(self, dimension: str):
0340 |         """Get training maximum score for normalization"""
0341 |         query = f"""
0342 |         SELECT MAX(score) FROM scoring_events
0343 |         WHERE dimension='{dimension}' AND source IN ('ebt', 'llm')
0344 |         """
0345 |         result = self.memory.db.execute(query).fetchone()
0346 |         return result[0] if result else 100
0347 | 
0348 |     async def run(self, context: dict) -> dict:
0349 |         """
0350 |         Main training loop for EBT refinement models
0351 |         """
0352 |         goal_text = context.get("goal", {}).get("goal_text")
0353 |         refinement_data = context.get("refinement_data", [])
0354 |         
0355 |         if not refinement_data:
0356 |             # Fetch from database if no data provided
0357 |             refinement_data = self._fetch_refinement_examples(goal_text)
0358 |         
0359 |         # Prepare data
0360 |         dataloaders = self.prepare_refinement_data(refinement_data)
0361 |         
0362 |         # Train per-dimension models
0363 |         trained_models = {}
0364 |         for dim, loader in dataloaders.items():
0365 |             self.logger.log("EBTRefinementStart", {
0366 |                 "dimension": dim,
0367 |                 "examples": len(loader.dataset)
0368 |             })
0369 |             
0370 |             trained_model = self.train_refinement_model(dim, loader)
0371 |             trained_models[dim] = trained_model.state_dict()
0372 |             
0373 |             # Update tuner
0374 |             if dim in self.tuners:
0375 |                 self._update_regression_tuner(loader, dim)
0376 |         
0377 |         # Update model registry
0378 |         self._update_model_registry(trained_models)
0379 |         
0380 |         context["trained_models"] = trained_models
0381 |         return context
0382 | 
0383 |     def _fetch_refinement_examples(self, goal: str = None) -> List[Dict]:
0384 |         """
0385 |         Fetch refinement examples from database
0386 |         """
0387 |         query = """
0388 |         SELECT * FROM refinement_events
0389 |         WHERE created_at > NOW() - INTERVAL '7 days'
0390 |         """
0391 |         if goal:
0392 |             query += f"AND context_hash = {hash(goal)}"
0393 |         
0394 |         results = self.memory.db.execute(query).fetchall()
0395 |         
0396 |         return [{
0397 |             "context": r.context,
0398 |             "original": r.original,
0399 |             "refined": r.refined,
0400 |             "dimension": r.dimension,
0401 |             "score": r.original_score,
0402 |             "refined_score": r.refined_score
0403 |         } for r in results]
0404 | 
0405 |     def _update_regression_tuner(self, dataloader: DataLoader, dimension: str):
0406 |         """Update regression tuner using refined examples"""
0407 |         for ctx, doc_a, doc_b, labels in dataloader:
0408 |             for i in range(len(ctx)):
0409 | 
0410 | 
0411 |                 llm_score = labels[i].cpu().item()
0412 |                 
0413 |                 # Update tuner with EBT-refined examples
0414 |                 self.tuners[dimension].train_single(
0415 |                     ebt_score=doc_b[i].item(),
0416 |                     llm_score=llm_score
0417 |                 )
0418 | 
0419 |     def _update_model_registry(self, trained_models: Dict[str, Dict]):
0420 |         """Update model registry with new versions"""
0421 |         for dim, state_dict in trained_models.items():
0422 |             self.logger.log("EBTModelUpdated", {
0423 |                 "dimension": dim,
0424 |                 "version": "auto",
0425 |                 "performance": self._evaluate_model(dim, state_dict)
0426 |             })

0435 |         }

0009 | def srft_collate_fn(batch: List[dict], embedding_store, device):
0010 |     """
0011 |     Collate function for SRFT refinement training.
0012 | 
0013 |     Embeds:
0014 |         - context
0015 |         - original
0016 |         - refined
0017 | 
0018 |     Returns:
0019 |         - context_tensor: (B, D)
0020 |         - original_tensor: (B, D)
0021 |         - refined_tensor: (B, D)
0022 |         - original_scores: (B,)
0023 |         - refined_scores: (B,)
0024 |         - original_energy: (B,)
0025 |         - refined_energy: (B,)
0026 |         - llm_scores: (B,) or None
0027 |         - uncertainty: (B,)
0028 |     """
0029 |     contexts = []
0030 |     originals = []
0031 |     refineds = []
0032 |     orig_scores, ref_scores = [], []
0033 |     orig_energy, ref_energy = [], []
0034 |     llm_scores = []
0035 |     uncertainties = []
0036 |

0039 |         originals.append(torch.tensor(embedding_store.get_or_create(item["original"])))

0041 |

0043 |         ref_scores.append(item["refined_score"])
0044 |         orig_energy.append(item["original_energy"])
0045 |         ref_energy.append(item["refined_energy"])
0046 |         uncertainties.append(item.get("uncertainty", 0.5))

0054 |         torch.tensor(ref_scores, dtype=torch.float32).to(device),
0055 |         torch.tensor(orig_energy, dtype=torch.float32).to(device),
0056 |         torch.tensor(ref_energy, dtype=torch.float32).to(device),
0057 |         torch.tensor(llm_scores, dtype=torch.float32).to(device),

0001 | # stephanie/agents/ebt/thinker.py
0002 | from __future__ import annotations
0003 | 
0004 | import torch
0005 | 
0006 | 
0007 | class EBTThinker:
0008 |     def __init__(self, model, step_size=0.05, steps=10):
0009 |         self.model = model
0010 |         self.step_size = step_size
0011 |         self.steps = steps
0012 | 
0013 |     def optimize(self, context_emb, initial_candidate):
0014 |         y = initial_candidate.clone().detach().requires_grad_(True)
0015 |         for _ in range(self.steps):
0016 |             energy = self.model(context_emb, y)
0017 |             grad = torch.autograd.grad(energy.sum(), y, create_graph=False)[0]
0018 |             y = y - self.step_size * grad
0019 |         return y.detach(), self.model(context_emb, y).item()
```

0001 | # stephanie/scoring/metrics/intelligent_frontier.py
0002 | from __future__ import annotations
0003 | 
0004 | import logging
0005 | from dataclasses import dataclass, field
0006 | from typing import Dict, List, Optional, Sequence, Tuple
0007 | 
0008 | import numpy as np
0009 | 
0010 | log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
0011 | 
0012 | 
0013 | @dataclass
0014 | class FrontierIntelligence:
0015 |     """
0016 |     Meta-controller for FrontierLens.
0017 | 
0018 |     Tracks how well individual metrics separate target vs baseline over time,
0019 |     and uses that (plus critic feedback) to choose a frontier metric.
0020 | 
0021 |     This is where learning *about* the metric space happens.
0022 |     """
0023 | 
0024 |     stability_window: int = 5
0025 |     alpha: float = 0.5     # weight on std (penalty)
0026 |     beta: float = 0.2      # weight on critic quality (bonus)
0027 | 
0028 |     # metric_name -> list of AUCs from past runs
0029 |     metric_history: Dict[str, List[float]] = field(default_factory=dict)
0030 |     # critic-wide quality scores (e.g., AUC over an eval set)
0031 |     critic_quality_history: List[float] = field(default_factory=list)
0032 | 
0033 |     # dynamically maintained list of core metrics
0034 |     core_metrics: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
0035 | 
0036 |     def update_metric_stability(
0037 |         self,
0038 |         metric_importance: List[Dict[str, float]],
0039 |         critic_quality_score: Optional[float] = None,
0040 |     ) -> None:
0041 |         """
0042 |         Log AUC stability per metric and optionally log critic-wide quality
0043 |         for this run.
0044 | 
0045 |         metric_importance:
0046 |             [
0047 |               {"metric": "sicql.coverage.score", "auc_roc": 0.91, ...},
0048 |               ...
0049 |             ]
0050 |         critic_quality_score:
0051 |             e.g., TinyCritic AUC over held-out eval for this run.
0052 |         """
0053 |         # Per-metric AUC history
0054 |         for metric in metric_importance:
0055 |             name = metric["metric"]
0056 |             auc = float(metric["auc_roc"])
0057 | 
0058 |             hist = self.metric_history.setdefault(name, [])
0059 |             hist.append(auc)
0060 |             # Trim history to stability window
0061 |             if len(hist) > self.stability_window:
0062 |                 hist.pop(0)
0063 | 
0064 |         # Critic quality history
0065 |         if critic_quality_score is not None:
0066 |             self.critic_quality_history.append(float(critic_quality_score))
0067 |             if len(self.critic_quality_history) > self.stability_window:
0068 |                 self.critic_quality_history.pop(0)
0069 | 
0070 |         self._update_core_metrics()
0071 | 
0072 |     def _update_core_metrics(self) -> None:
0073 |         """
0074 |         Identify the most stable, useful metrics across runs.
0075 | 
0076 |         Score:
0077 |             stability_score = avg_auc
0078 |                               - alpha * std_auc
0079 |                               + beta  * avg_critic_quality
0080 |         """
0081 |         stable_metrics: List[Tuple[str, float, float, float]] = []
0082 | 
0083 |         avg_critic_quality = (
0084 |             float(np.mean(self.critic_quality_history))
0085 |             if self.critic_quality_history
0086 |             else 0.5
0087 |         )
0088 | 
0089 |         for metric, scores in self.metric_history.items():
0090 |             # skip special key
0091 |             if metric == "critic_quality":
0092 |                 continue
0093 | 
0094 |             if len(scores) < max(2, self.stability_window // 2):
0095 |                 continue
0096 | 
0097 |             scores_arr = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
0098 |             stability = float(scores_arr.std())
0099 |             avg_auc = float(scores_arr.mean())
0100 | 
0101 |             stability_score = (
0102 |                 avg_auc
0103 |                 - self.alpha * stability
0104 |                 + self.beta * avg_critic_quality
0105 |             )
0106 |             stable_metrics.append((metric, stability_score, avg_auc, stability))
0107 | 
0108 |         # Sort by stability_score descending
0109 |         stable_metrics.sort(key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)
0110 |         self.core_metrics = [m[0] for m in stable_metrics[: max(5, len(stable_metrics) // 3)]]
0111 | 
0112 |         if self.core_metrics:
0113 |             log.info(
0114 |                 "FrontierIntelligence: updated core_metrics (%d): %s%s",
0115 |                 len(self.core_metrics),
0116 |                 ", ".join(self.core_metrics[:3]),
0117 |                 "..." if len(self.core_metrics) > 3 else "",
0118 |             )
0119 |         else:
0120 |             log.warning(
0121 |                 "FrontierIntelligence: no stable metrics yet "
0122 |                 "(need more runs or labels)."
0123 |             )
0124 | 
0125 |     def select_frontier_metric(
0126 |         self,
0127 |         candidate_metrics: Sequence[str],
0128 |         fallback: Optional[str] = None,
0129 |     ) -> str:
0130 |         """
0131 |         Choose the best frontier metric from the candidate list.
0132 | 
0133 |         Preference order:
0134 |           1) First core metric that appears in candidate_metrics,
0135 |           2) explicit fallback,
0136 |           3) first candidate.
0137 |         """
0138 |         cand_set = set(candidate_metrics)
0139 | 
0140 |         # Prefer learned core metrics
0141 |         for m in self.core_metrics:
0142 |             if m in cand_set:
0143 |                 log.info("FrontierIntelligence: selected frontier_metric=%r", m)
0144 |                 return m
0145 | 
0146 |         # Fallbacks
0147 |         if fallback and fallback in cand_set:
0148 |             log.warning(
0149 |                 "FrontierIntelligence: no core metrics in candidate set; "
0150 |                 "using fallback=%r",
0151 |                 fallback,
0152 |             )
0153 |             return fallback
0154 | 
0155 |         if candidate_metrics:
0156 |             log.warning(
0157 |                 "FrontierIntelligence: no core metrics; using first candidate=%r",
0158 |                 candidate_metrics[0],
0159 |             )
0160 |             return candidate_metrics[0]
0161 | 
0162 |         raise ValueError("FrontierIntelligence.select_frontier_metric: no candidate_metrics provided")
0163 | 
0164 | 
0165 | def compute_dynamic_bands(
0166 |     frontier_values: np.ndarray,
0167 |     target_good_ratio: float = 0.4,
0168 |     min_band_size: int = 5,
0169 | ) -> Tuple[float, float, float]:
0170 |     """
0171 |     Dynamically adjust band boundaries based on the empirical distribution
0172 |     of the frontier metric.
0173 | 
0174 |     Args:
0175 |         frontier_values:
0176 |             1D array of frontier metric values for all examples
0177 |             (already normalized into [0,1] is ideal).
0178 |         target_good_ratio:
0179 |             Desired fraction of examples in the "good" band.
0180 |         min_band_size:
0181 |             Minimum #examples on each side (below and above the band).
0182 | 
0183 |     Returns:
0184 |         (low_threshold, high_threshold, actual_good_ratio)
0185 |     """
0186 |     vals = np.asarray(frontier_values, dtype=np.float64)
0187 |     vals = vals[np.isfinite(vals)]
0188 |     if vals.size == 0:
0189 |         # degenerate case: no finite data
0190 |         log.warning(
0191 |             "compute_dynamic_bands: no finite frontier_values; using default [0.25, 0.75]."
0192 |         )
0193 |         return 0.25, 0.75, 0.5
0194 | 
0195 |     vals.sort()
0196 |     n = vals.size
0197 | 
0198 |     # Ideal indices assuming symmetric tails for "bad"
0199 |     tail_fraction = (1.0 - float(target_good_ratio)) / 2.0
0200 |     low_idx = max(min_band_size, int(n * tail_fraction))
0201 |     high_idx = min(n - min_band_size, n - int(n * tail_fraction))
0202 | 
0203 |     # Safety clamps
0204 |     low_idx = max(0, min(low_idx, n - 1))
0205 |     high_idx = max(low_idx + 1, min(high_idx, n - 1))
0206 | 
0207 |     low_threshold = float(vals[low_idx])
0208 |     high_threshold = float(vals[high_idx])
0209 | 
0210 |     # Compute actual achieved good ratio Currently it's distributed across these files
0211 |     mask_good = (vals >= low_threshold) & (vals <= high_threshold)
0212 |     actual_good_ratio = float(mask_good.mean())
0213 | 
0214 |     if high_threshold <= low_threshold:
0215 |         log.warning(
0216 |             "compute_dynamic_bands: degenerate thresholds (low=%.3f, high=%.3f); "
0217 |             "falling back to [0.25, 0.75].",
0218 |             low_threshold,
0219 |             high_threshold,
0220 |         )
0221 |         low_threshold, high_threshold = 0.25, 0.75
0222 |         actual_good_ratio = 0.5
0223 | 
0224 |     log.info(
0225 |         "FrontierIntelligence: dynamic bands [%.3f, %.3f] "
0226 |         "(target_good_ratio=%.2f, actual_good_ratio=%.2f, n=%d)",
0227 |         low_threshold,
0228 |         high_threshold,
0229 |         target_good_ratio,
0230 |         actual_good_ratio,
0231 |         n,
0232 |     )
0233 | 
0234 |     return low_threshold, high_threshold, actual_good_ratio
```

0365 | 
0366 | def normalize_scores(scores: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-8) -> np.ndarray:
0367 |     """
0368 |     Normalize each metric column to [0,1] across items.
0369 |     If a column is constant, it becomes 0.5.
0370 |     """
0371 |     scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
0372 |     if scores.ndim != 2:
0373 |         raise ValueError(f"Expected 2D scores, got {scores.shape}")
0374 | 
0375 |     out = np.zeros_like(scores, dtype=np.float64)
0376 |     for j in range(scores.shape[1]):
0377 |         col = scores[:, j]
0378 |         cmin = float(col.min())
0379 |         cmax = float(col.max())
0380 |         if cmax - cmin < eps:
0381 |             out[:, j] = 0.5
0382 |         else:
0383 |             out[:, j] = (col - cmin) / (cmax - cmin)
0384 |     return out
0385 | 
0386 | 
0387 | def scores_to_vpm_uint8(
0388 |     scores: np.ndarray,
0389 |     *,
0390 |     per_metric_normalize: bool = True,
0391 |     eps: float = 1e-8,
0392 | ) -> np.ndarray:
0393 |     """
0394 |     Convert a 2D scores matrix into a [0,255] uint8 image.
0395 | 
0396 |     - per_metric_normalize=True:
0397 |         normalize each metric column to [0,1] (like normalize_scores)
0398 |     - per_metric_normalize=False:
0399 |         global min–max across the whole matrix.
0400 |     """
0401 |     arr = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
0402 |     if arr.ndim != 2:
0403 |         raise ValueError(f"scores_to_vpm_uint8: expected 2D, got shape {arr.shape}")
0404 | 
0405 |     if per_metric_normalize:
0406 |         arr = normalize_scores(arr, eps=eps)
0407 |     else:
0408 |         cmin = float(np.nanmin(arr))
0409 |         cmax = float(np.nanmax(arr))
0410 |         if not np.isfinite(cmin) or not np.isfinite(cmax):
0411 |             arr = np.nan_to_num(arr, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=0.0)
0412 |             cmin = float(arr.min())
0413 |             cmax = float(arr.max())
0414 |         if cmax - cmin < eps:
0415 |             arr = np.zeros_like(arr) + 0.5
0416 |         else:
0417 |             arr = (arr - cmin) / (cmax - cmin)
0418 | 
0419 |     # Clean up NaNs/Infs and clip to [0,1]
0420 |     arr = np.nan_to_num(arr, nan=0.0, posinf=1.0, neginf=0.0)
0421 |     arr = np.clip(arr, 0.0, 1.0)
0422 | 
0423 |     img = (arr * 255.0).round().astype(np.uint8)  # shape: (N_rows, N_metrics)
0424 |     return img
0425 | 
0426 | 
0427 | def compute_frontier_mask(
0428 |     scores: np.ndarray,
0429 |     low: float = 0.25,
0430 |     high: float = 0.75,
0431 | ) -> np.ndarray:
0432 |     """
0433 |     Frontier band: entries whose value lies in [low, high].
0434 |     Returns a boolean mask of same shape as scores.
0435 |     """
0436 |     scores = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float64)
0437 |     if scores.ndim != 2:
0438 |         raise ValueError(f"Expected 2D scores, got {scores.shape}")
0439 |     if not (0.0 <= low <= high <= 1.0):
0440 |         raise ValueError(f"Invalid band [{low}, {high}], must be in [0,1] with low <= high")
0441 | 
0442 |     return (scores >= low) & (scores <= high)
0443 | 
0444 | 
0445 | def row_entropy(prob_row: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-8) -> float:
0446 |     """
0447 |     Shannon entropy of a row of non-negative values, treated as a distribution.
0448 |     We renormalize the row to sum to 1.
0449 |     """
0450 |     p = np.asarray(prob_row, dtype=np.float64)
0451 |     p = np.maximum(p, 0.0)
0452 |     s = float(p.sum())
0453 |     if s < eps:
0454 |         return 0.0
0455 |     p = p / s
0456 |     mask = p > eps
0457 |     return float(-np.sum(p[mask] * np.log(p[mask] + eps)))
0458 | 
0459 | 
0460 | def episode_summary(
0461 |     episode: FrontierLensEpisode,
0462 |     frontier_band: Tuple[float, float] = (0.25, 0.75),
0463 | ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
0464 |     """
0465 |     Produce a dictionary of summary stats for an episode.
0466 |     You can log this or turn it into features later.
0467 |     """
0468 |     scores_norm = normalize_scores(episode.scores)
0469 |     low, high = frontier_band
0470 |     frontier_mask = compute_frontier_mask(scores_norm, low=low, high=high)
0471 | 
0472 |     N, M = scores_norm.shape
0473 | 
0474 |     # Per-metric stats
0475 |     means = scores_norm.mean(axis=0)
0476 |     stds = scores_norm.std(axis=0)
0477 | 
0478 |     # Frontier coverage
0479 |     frontier_fraction = frontier_mask.mean()          # global fraction
0480 |     frontier_per_metric = frontier_mask.mean(axis=0)  # per metric
0481 | 
0482 |     # Row entropies (treat each row as distribution over metrics)
0483 |     row_entropies = np.array([row_entropy(scores_norm[i, :]) for i in range(N)])
0484 |     mean_row_entropy = float(row_entropies.mean()) if len(row_entropies) else 0.0
0485 |     std_row_entropy = float(row_entropies.std()) if len(row_entropies) else 0.0
0486 | 
0487 |     return {
0488 |         "episode_id": episode.episode_id,
0489 |         "n_items": N,
0490 |         "n_metrics": M,
0491 |         "metric_names": list(episode.metric_names),
0492 |         "mean_per_metric": means,
0493 |         "std_per_metric": stds,
0494 |         "frontier_fraction": float(frontier_fraction),
0495 |         "frontier_per_metric": frontier_per_metric,
0496 |         "mean_row_entropy": mean_row_entropy,
0497 |         "std_row_entropy": std_row_entropy,
0498 |         "frontier_band": (low, high),
0499 |     }
0500 | 
0501 | 
0502 | def episode_features(
0503 |     episode: FrontierLensEpisode,
0504 |     frontier_band: Tuple[float, float] = (0.25, 0.75),
0505 | ) -> Tuple[np.ndarray, List[str]]:
0506 |     """
0507 |     Turn an episode into a fixed-length feature vector + feature names.
0508 | 
0509 |     Current design (for M metrics):
0510 |       - mean_per_metric (M)
0511 |       - std_per_metric (M)
0512 |       - frontier_per_metric (M)
0513 |       - frontier_fraction (1)
0514 |       - mean_row_entropy (1)
0515 |       - std_row_entropy (1)
0516 |     => total dim = 3M + 3
0517 |     """
0518 |     summary = episode_summary(episode, frontier_band=frontier_band)
0519 |     metric_names = summary["metric_names"]
0520 | 
0521 |     mean_per_metric = np.asarray(summary["mean_per_metric"], dtype=np.float64)
0522 |     std_per_metric = np.asarray(summary["std_per_metric"], dtype=np.float64)
0523 |     frontier_per_metric = np.asarray(summary["frontier_per_metric"], dtype=np.float64)
0524 | 
0525 |     feats = np.concatenate(
0526 |         [
0527 |             mean_per_metric,
0528 |             std_per_metric,
0529 |             frontier_per_metric,
0530 |             np.array(
0531 |                 [
0532 |                     summary["frontier_fraction"],
0533 |                     summary["mean_row_entropy"],
0534 |                     summary["std_row_entropy"],
0535 |                 ],
0536 |                 dtype=np.float64,
0537 |             ),
0538 |         ],
0539 |         axis=0,
0540 |     )
0541 | 
0542 |     # Feature names
0543 |     feat_names: List[str] = []
0544 |     for name in metric_names:
0545 |         feat_names.append(f"mean[{name}]")
0546 |     for name in metric_names:
0547 |         feat_names.append(f"std[{name}]")
0548 |     for name in metric_names:
0549 |         feat_names.append(f"frontier[{name}]")
0550 |     feat_names.extend(
0551 |         [
0552 |             "frontier_global",
0553 |             "mean_row_entropy",
0554 |             "std_row_entropy",
0555 |         ]
0556 |     )
0557 | 
0558 |     return feats.astype(np.float32), feat_names
0559 | 
0560 | 
0561 | # =========================================================================== #
0562 | # 3. Core computation: compute_frontier_lens_report (with visicalc alias)
0563 | # =========================================================================== #
0564 | 
0565 | 
0566 | def compute_frontier_lens_report(
0567 |     vpm: np.ndarray,
0568 |     metric_names: Sequence[str],
0569 |     frontier_metric: str,
0570 |     row_region_splits: int,
0571 |     frontier_low: float = 0.25,
0572 |     frontier_high: float = 0.75,
0573 | ) -> FrontierLensReport:
0574 |     """
0575 |     Pure computation: build a FrontierLensReport from a raw score matrix.
0576 | 
0577 |     vpm:
0578 |         (N_items, N_metrics) score matrix, ideally normalized to [0,1]
0579 |     metric_names:
0580 |         length-N_metrics list of metric names
0581 |     frontier_metric:
0582 |         which metric to treat as the "frontier" dimension
0583 |     row_region_splits:
0584 |         how many contiguous row regions to divide the items into
0585 |     frontier_low/high:
0586 |         band defining the frontier for coverage stats
0587 |     """
0588 |     vpm = np.asarray(vpm, dtype=np.float64)
0589 |     if vpm.ndim != 2:
0590 |         raise ValueError(f"vpm must be 2D, got shape {vpm.shape}")
0591 | 
0592 |     num_rows, num_metrics = vpm.shape
0593 |     metric_names = list(metric_names)
0594 | 
0595 |     if num_rows == 0 or num_metrics == 0:
0596 |         report = FrontierLensReport(
0597 |             frontier_metric=frontier_metric,
0598 |             frontier_low=frontier_low,
0599 |             frontier_high=frontier_high,
0600 |             row_region_splits=row_region_splits,
0601 |             regions=[],
0602 |             global_frontier_frac=0.0,
0603 |             global_low_frac=0.0,
0604 |             global_high_frac=0.0,
0605 |         )
0606 |         report.validate()
0607 |         return report
0608 | 
0609 |     # Select frontier column
0610 |     try:
0611 |         fm_idx = metric_names.index(frontier_metric)
0612 |     except ValueError:
0613 |         log.warning(
0614 |             "Frontier metric '%s' not found; using first metric '%s'",
0615 |             frontier_metric,
0616 |             metric_names[0],
0617 |         )
0618 |         fm_idx = 0
0619 |         frontier_metric = metric_names[0]
0620 | 
0621 |     frontier_vals = vpm[:, fm_idx]
0622 |     low, high = float(frontier_low), float(frontier_high)
0623 | 
0624 |     if not (0.0 <= low < high <= 1.0):
0625 |         raise ValueError(f"Invalid frontier band [{low}, {high}]")
0626 | 
0627 |     # Global stats over the entire matrix
0628 |     g_mean = float(vpm.mean())
0629 |     g_std = float(vpm.std())
0630 |     g_min = float(vpm.min())
0631 |     g_max = float(vpm.max())
0632 | 
0633 |     band_mask = (frontier_vals >= low) & (frontier_vals <= high)
0634 |     global_frontier_frac = float(band_mask.mean())
0635 |     global_low_frac = float((frontier_vals < low).mean())
0636 |     global_high_frac = float((frontier_vals > high).mean())
0637 | 
0638 |     # Sparsity (approximate "how much of the matrix is near zero")
0639 |     sparsity_e3 = float(np.mean(vpm <= 1e-3))
0640 |     sparsity_e2 = float(np.mean(vpm <= 1e-2))
0641 | 
0642 |     # Entropy of the scalar distribution
0643 |     hist, _ = np.histogram(vpm, bins=32, range=(0.0, 1.0), density=True)
0644 |     hist = hist[hist > 0]
0645 |     if len(hist) > 0:
0646 |         entropy = float(-np.sum(hist * np.log(hist)) / np.log(len(hist)))
0647 |     else:
0648 |         entropy = 0.0
0649 | 
0650 |     # Row region bounds: split rows as evenly as possible
0651 |     splits = int(row_region_splits)
0652 |     base, rem = divmod(num_rows, splits)
0653 |     bounds: List[Tuple[int, int]] = []
0654 |     start = 0
0655 |     for i in range(splits):
0656 |         end = start + base + (1 if i < rem else 0)
0657 |         bounds.append((start, end))
0658 |         start = end
0659 | 
0660 |     regions: List[FrontierLensRegion] = []
0661 |     for i, (rs, re) in enumerate(bounds):
0662 |         if rs >= re:
0663 |             regions.append(
0664 |                 FrontierLensRegion(
0665 |                     index=i,
0666 |                     start_row=rs,
0667 |                     end_row=re,
0668 |                     row_count=0,
0669 |                     frontier_frac=0.0,
0670 |                     low_frac=0.0,
0671 |                     high_frac=0.0,
0672 |                     mean_frontier_value=0.0,
0673 |                 )
0674 |             )
0675 |             continue
0676 | 
0677 |         seg_vals = frontier_vals[rs:re]
0678 |         seg_mask = band_mask[rs:re]
0679 |         regions.append(
0680 |             FrontierLensRegion(
0681 |                 index=i,
0682 |                 start_row=rs,
0683 |                 end_row=re,
0684 |                 row_count=re - rs,
0685 |                 frontier_frac=float(seg_mask.mean()),
0686 |                 low_frac=float((seg_vals < low).mean()),
0687 |                 high_frac=float((seg_vals > high).mean()),
0688 |                 mean_frontier_value=float(seg_vals.mean()),
0689 |             )
0690 |         )
0691 | 
0692 |     report = FrontierLensReport(
0693 |         frontier_metric=frontier_metric,
0694 |         frontier_low=low,
0695 |         frontier_high=high,
0696 |         row_region_splits=splits,
0697 |         regions=regions,
0698 |         global_frontier_frac=global_frontier_frac,
0699 |         global_low_frac=global_low_frac,
0700 |         global_high_frac=global_high_frac,
0701 |         global_mean=g_mean,
0702 |         global_std=g_std,
0703 |         global_min=g_min,
0704 |         global_max=g_max,
0705 |         entropy=entropy,
0706 |         sparsity_level_e3=sparsity_e3,
0707 |         sparsity_level_e2=sparsity_e2,
0708 |     )
0709 |     report.validate()
0710 |     return report
0711 | 
0712 | 
0713 | # =========================================================================== #
0714 | # 4. Main Class: FrontierLens
0715 | # =========================================================================== #
0716 | 
0717 | 
0718 | @dataclass
0719 | class FrontierLens:
0720 |     """
0721 |     Unified analyzer for cognitive metrics over sequences of scored items (e.g., Scorables).
0722 | 
0723 |     Turns a list of scored items into:
0724 |       - a FrontierLensReport (structured summary)
0725 |       - a fixed-length feature vector (for ML models)
0726 |       - a scalar quality score
0727 |       - a diff vs another state
0728 | 
0729 |     Use cases:
0730 |       - Compare graph states before/after Blossom expansion
0731 |       - Measure reasoning coherence in Nexus episodes
0732 |       - Track idea evolution in filmstrip visualizations
0733 |     """
0734 | 
0735 |     episode_id: str
0736 |     scores: np.ndarray           # (N_items, N_metrics)
0737 |     metric_names: List[str]
0738 |     item_ids: List[str]
0739 |     frontier_metric: str
0740 |     row_region_splits: int = 3
0741 |     frontier_low: float = 0.25
0742 |     frontier_high: float = 0.75
0743 |     meta: Dict[str, Any] = field(default_factory=dict)
0744 | 
0745 |     # Computed during __post_init__
0746 |     report: Optional[FrontierLensReport] = None
0747 |     features: Optional[np.ndarray] = None
0748 |     feature_names: Optional[List[str]] = None
0749 | 
0750 |     def __post_init__(self):
0751 |         scores = np.asarray(self.scores)
0752 |         if scores.ndim != 2:
0753 |             raise ValueError(f"scores must be 2D, got shape {scores.shape}")
0754 |         if len(self.metric_names) != scores.shape[1]:
0755 |             raise ValueError("metric_names length mismatch")
0756 |         if len(self.item_ids) != scores.shape[0]:
0757 |             raise ValueError("item_ids length mismatch")
0758 | 
0759 |         self.scores = scores
0760 | 
0761 |         # Build derived outputs
0762 |         self.report = compute_frontier_lens_report(
0763 |             vpm=self.scores,
0764 |             metric_names=self.metric_names,
0765 |             frontier_metric=self.frontier_metric,
0766 |             row_region_splits=self.row_region_splits,
0767 |             frontier_low=self.frontier_low,
0768 |             frontier_high=self.frontier_high,
0769 |         )
0770 |         episode = FrontierLensEpisode(
0771 |             episode_id=self.episode_id,
0772 |             scores=self.scores,
0773 |             metric_names=self.metric_names,
0774 |             item_ids=self.item_ids,
0775 |             meta=self.meta,
0776 |         )
0777 |         feats, names = episode_features(episode, frontier_band=(self.frontier_low, self.frontier_high))
0778 |         self.features = feats
0779 |         self.feature_names = names
0780 | 
0781 |     # =============================
0782 |     # Public API
0783 |     # =============================
0784 | 
0785 |     @classmethod
0786 |     def from_rows(
0787 |         cls,
0788 |         *,
0789 |         episode_id: str,
0790 |         rows: List[Dict[str, Any]],
0791 |         frontier_metric: str,
0792 |         row_region_splits: int = 3,
0793 |         frontier_low: float = 0.25,
0794 |         frontier_high: float = 0.75,
0795 |         meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
0796 |     ) -> "FrontierLens":
0797 |         """
0798 |         Build from ScorableProcessor-style rows.
0799 | 
0800 |         Each row must have:
0801 |           - 'scorable_id'
0802 |           - 'metrics_columns': List[str]
0803 |           - 'metrics_values': List[float]
0804 |         """
0805 |         if not rows:
0806 |             raise ValueError("FrontierLens.from_rows: no rows provided")
0807 | 
0808 |         first = rows[0]
0809 |         metric_names = list(first.get("metrics_columns") or [])
0810 |         if not metric_names:
0811 |             raise ValueError("FrontierLens.from_rows: first row missing 'metrics_columns'")
0812 | 
0813 |         matrix_rows: List[List[float]] = []
0814 |         item_ids: List[str] = []
0815 | 
0816 |         for row in rows:
0817 |             vals = row.get("metrics_values")
0818 |             if not vals:
0819 |                 continue
0820 |             mapping = dict(zip(row.get("metrics_columns", []), vals))
0821 |             vec = [float(mapping.get(m, 0.0)) for m in metric_names]
0822 |             matrix_rows.append(vec)
0823 |             item_ids.append(str(row.get("scorable_id", "unknown")))
0824 | 
0825 |         if not matrix_rows:
0826 |             raise ValueError("FrontierLens.from_rows: no valid rows with metrics_values")
0827 | 
0828 |         X = np.array(matrix_rows, dtype=np.float32)
0829 | 
0830 |         fm = frontier_metric if frontier_metric in metric_names else metric_names[0]
0831 | 
0832 |         return cls(
0833 |             episode_id=episode_id,
0834 |             scores=X,
0835 |             metric_names=metric_names,
0836 |             item_ids=item_ids,
0837 |             frontier_metric=fm,
0838 |             row_region_splits=row_region_splits,
0839 |             frontier_low=frontier_low,
0840 |             frontier_high=frontier_high,
0841 |             meta=meta or {},
0842 |         )
0843 | 
0844 |     @classmethod
0845 |     def from_matrix(
0846 |         cls,
0847 |         *,
0848 |         episode_id: str,
0849 |         scores: Union[np.ndarray, Sequence[Sequence[float]]],
0850 |         metric_names: Sequence[str],
0851 |         item_ids: Sequence[str],
0852 |         frontier_metric: Optional[str] = None,
0853 |         row_region_splits: int = 3,
0854 |         frontier_low: float = 0.25,
0855 |         frontier_high: float = 0.75,
0856 |         meta: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
0857 |     ) -> "FrontierLens":
0858 |         """
0859 |         Build a FrontierLens instance directly from a score matrix.
0860 | 
0861 |         Args:
0862 |             episode_id:
0863 |                 Logical id for this episode (e.g. "frontier_lens:targeted").
0864 |             scores:
0865 |                 2D array-like of shape (N_items, N_metrics).
0866 |             metric_names:
0867 |                 Length-N_metrics sequence of metric names (column order).
0868 |             item_ids:
0869 |                 Length-N_items sequence of ids for each row (e.g. scorable_ids).
0870 |             frontier_metric:
0871 |                 Which metric to treat as the 'frontier' dimension.
0872 |                 If None or not found, falls back to the first metric.
0873 |             row_region_splits:
0874 |                 How many contiguous row regions to divide items into.
0875 |             frontier_low / frontier_high:
0876 |                 Frontier band in normalized [0, 1] space.
0877 |             meta:
0878 |                 Optional extra metadata to carry along.
0879 | 
0880 |         Returns:
0881 |             FrontierLens instance with .report, .features, .feature_names populated.
0882 |         """
0883 |         X = np.asarray(scores, dtype=np.float32)
0884 |         if X.ndim != 2:
0885 |             raise ValueError(f"FrontierLens.from_matrix: scores must be 2D, got shape {X.shape}")
0886 | 
0887 |         n_items, n_metrics = X.shape
0888 |         metric_names_list = list(metric_names)
0889 |         item_ids_list = [str(i) for i in item_ids]
0890 | 
0891 |         if len(metric_names_list) != n_metrics:
0892 |             raise ValueError(
0893 |                 f"FrontierLens.from_matrix: metric_names length {len(metric_names_list)} "
0894 |                 f"!= scores.shape[1] {n_metrics}"
0895 |             )
0896 | 
0897 |         if len(item_ids_list) != n_items:
0898 |             raise ValueError(
0899 |                 f"FrontierLens.from_matrix: item_ids length {len(item_ids_list)} "
0900 |                 f"!= scores.shape[0] {n_items}"
0901 |             )
0902 | 
0903 |         # Resolve frontier metric
0904 |         fm = frontier_metric
0905 |         if not fm or fm not in metric_names_list:
0906 |             if fm is not None:
0907 |                 log.warning(
0908 |                     "FrontierLens.from_matrix: requested frontier_metric=%r not in metric_names=%r; "
0909 |                     "falling back to first metric",
0910 |                     fm,
0911 |                     metric_names_list,
0912 |                 )
0913 |             fm = metric_names_list[0]
0914 | 
0915 |         return cls(
0916 |             episode_id=episode_id,
0917 |             scores=X,
0918 |             metric_names=metric_names_list,
0919 |             item_ids=item_ids_list,
0920 |             frontier_metric=fm,
0921 |             row_region_splits=row_region_splits,
0922 |             frontier_low=float(frontier_low),
0923 |             frontier_high=float(frontier_high),
0924 |             meta=meta or {},
0925 |         )
0926 | 
0927 |     def quality(self, low_weight: float = 0.5, high_weight: float = 0.5) -> float:
0928 |         """Scalar quality score for this episode."""
0929 |         return self.report.quality_score(low_weight=low_weight, high_weight=high_weight)
0930 | 
0931 |     def diff(self, baseline: "FrontierLens") -> Dict[str, Any]:
0932 |         """
0933 |         Compare this state to a baseline.
0934 | 
0935 |         Returns a dict with:
0936 |           - 'frontier_metric'
0937 |           - 'band'
0938 |           - 'target_splits' / 'baseline_splits'
0939 |           - 'global_delta'
0940 |           - 'regions'
0941 |           - 'quality_delta'
0942 |           - 'feature_sim'
0943 |         """
0944 |         report_delta = self.report.diff(baseline.report)
0945 | 
0946 |         # Add extra top-level deltas
0947 |         quality_delta = self.quality() - baseline.quality()
0948 |         # cos-sim between feature vectors
0949 |         num = float(np.dot(self.features, baseline.features))
0950 |         den = float(np.linalg.norm(self.features) * np.linalg.norm(baseline.features) + 1e-8)
0951 |         feature_sim = num / den if den > 0 else 0.0
0952 | 
0953 |         report_delta["quality_delta"] = quality_delta
0954 |         report_delta["feature_sim"] = feature_sim
0955 |         report_delta["target_episode_id"] = self.episode_id
0956 |         report_delta["baseline_episode_id"] = baseline.episode_id
0957 |         return report_delta
0958 | 
0959 |     def save_report(self, path: Union[Path, str]) -> Path:
0960 |         """Save just the report to JSON."""
0961 |         return self.report.save_json(path)
0962 | 
0963 |     def to_vpm_array(
0964 |         self,
0965 |         *,
0966 |         per_metric_normalize: bool = True,
0967 |     ) -> np.ndarray:
0968 |         """
0969 |         Return a uint8 VPM array (N_items × N_metrics) suitable for saving
0970 |         as a PNG or feeding into ZeroModel / tiny vision models.
0971 |         """
0972 |         return scores_to_vpm_uint8(
0973 |             self.scores,
0974 |             per_metric_normalize=per_metric_normalize,
0975 |         )
0976 | 
0977 |     def save_vpm_png(
0978 |         self,
0979 |         path: Union[Path, str],
0980 |         *,
0981 |         per_metric_normalize: bool = True,
0982 |         mode: str = "L",
0983 |     ) -> Path:
0984 |         """
0985 |         Save the episode's scores as a VPM PNG.
0986 | 
0987 |         - mode="L": grayscale (items = vertical axis, metrics = horizontal).
0988 |         - mode="RGB": replicate grayscale into 3 channels.
0989 |         """
0990 |         img_arr = self.to_vpm_array(per_metric_normalize=per_metric_normalize)
0991 |         p = Path(path)
0992 |         p.parent.mkdir(parents=True, exist_ok=True)
0993 | 
0994 |         if mode.upper() == "L":
0995 |             img = Image.fromarray(img_arr, mode="L")
0996 |         else:
0997 |             if img_arr.ndim == 2:
0998 |                 rgb = np.stack([img_arr] * 3, axis=-1)
0999 |             else:
1000 |                 rgb = img_arr

0339 |     def _safe_minmax(self, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:

0400 |     def _minmax_normalize_safe(self, X: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
0401 |         Xn = X.astype(float, copy=True)
0402 |         mins = Xn.min(axis=0)

0409 |         np.clip(Xn, 0.0, 1.0, out=Xn)

0421 |             if isinstance(n, (list, tuple)):
0422 |                 if len(n) == 0:
0423 |                     dropped += 1

0425 |                 n = n[0]
0426 |             if not isinstance(n, str):

0436 |     def _variance_keep_mask(self, X: np.ndarray, min_var: float) -> np.ndarray:
0437 |         """
0438 |         Return a boolean mask of columns whose (NaN-safe) variance >= min_var.
0439 | 
0440 |         - Works for any 2D array-like (treats NaNs as missing).
0441 |         - Non-finite variances are treated as 0 to avoid crashes.
0442 |         """
0443 |         X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
0444 |         if X.ndim != 2:
0445 |             X = np.atleast_2d(X)
0446 | 
0447 |         # NaN-safe variance per column
0448 |         with np.errstate(invalid="ignore"):
0449 |             col_var = np.nanvar(X, axis=0)
0450 | 
0451 |         # Replace non-finite with 0 so we can compare safely
0452 |         col_var = np.where(np.isfinite(col_var), col_var, 0.0)

0456 |     def _variance_rank_and_cut(
0457 |         self,
0458 |         names: List[str],

0464 |         largest NaN-safe variance. Stable and deterministic.
0465 | 
0466 |         - If top_k is None/<=0 or >= num_cols, returns inputs unchanged.
0467 |         - Non-finite variances treated as 0 to avoid crashes.
0468 |         """
0469 |         X = np.asarray(X, dtype=float)
0470 |         if X.ndim != 2:
0471 |             X = np.atleast_2d(X)
0472 | 
0473 |         n_cols = X.shape[1]

0475 |             return [], X
0476 | 
0477 |         k = int(top_k) if (top_k is not None and int(top_k) > 0) else n_cols

0481 | 
0482 |         # NaN-safe variance per column

0491 |         kept_names = [names[i] for i in sel_idx]

0040 |     frac1 = float(np.mean(np.isclose(x_ok, 1.0))) if x_ok.size else float("nan")

0055 |         try:

0100 |     kept_set = set(kept_names)

0102 |     lowvar_set = set(int(i) for i in lowvar_idx)
0103 |     dup_dropped_map = {}  # dropped -> (kept, sim)
0104 |     for kept, dropped, sim in dup_pairs:

0117 |             reason = "low-variance"
0118 |         elif n in dup_dropped_map:

0124 |             reason = "dropped"
0125 |         diags.append(ColumnDiag(
0126 |             name=n, kept=(n in kept_set), reason=reason,

0128 |         ))

0136 |         for d in diags:
0137 |             w.writerow([d.name, int(d.kept), d.reason, d.variance, d.min, d.max, d.frac_zeros, d.frac_ones, d.auc if d.auc is not None else "", d.mi if d.mi is not None else ""])
0138 | 
0139 |     # Headline stats
0140 |     kept_hrm = sum(1 for d in diags if d.kept and d.name.lower().startswith("hrm"))
0141 |     kept_sicql = sum(1 for d in diags if d.kept and d.name.lower().startswith("sicql"))
0142 |     kept_tiny = sum(1 for d in diags if d.kept and d.name.lower().startswith("tiny"))
0143 | 
0144 |     # Markdown
0145 |     md_path = run_dir / md_filename

0147 |     total = len(names_union)
0148 |     kept_ct = len(kept_names)
0149 |     dropped_ct = total - kept_ct

0151 |     most_ones = sorted(diags, key=lambda d: (math.isnan(d.frac_ones), -d.frac_ones))[:10]
0152 |     most_zeros = sorted(diags, key=lambda d: (math.isnan(d.frac_zeros), -d.frac_zeros))[:10]

0157 |         f.write(f"- **Dropped**: {dropped_ct}\n")
0158 |         f.write(f"- **Normalize to [0,1]**: {normalize_used}\n")
0159 |         f.write(f"- **Ranking method**: {rank_method}\n")

0165 |         f.write("\n## Kept by family\n")

0167 |         f.write(f"- SICQL: {kept_sicql}\n")
0168 |         f.write(f"- Tiny: {kept_tiny}\n")

0170 |         f.write("\n## Duplicate drops (sample)\n")

0173 | 
0174 |         f.write("\n## High-probably-saturated columns (top frac=1.0)\n")
0175 |         for d in most_ones:

0177 |                 f.write(f"- `{d.name}` frac_ones={d.frac_ones:.3f} var={d.variance:.2e}\n")

0179 |         f.write("\n## High-probably-dead columns (top frac=0.0)\n")

0001 | # stephanie/scoring/metrics/metric_importance.py
0002 | from __future__ import annotations
0003 | 
0004 | import json
0005 | import math
0006 | from dataclasses import asdict, dataclass
0007 | from pathlib import Path
0008 | from typing import Any, Dict, List, Sequence, Tuple
0009 | 
0010 | import numpy as np
0011 | 
0012 | 
0013 | @dataclass
0014 | class MetricImportance:
0015 |     name: str
0016 |     mean_target: float
0017 |     mean_baseline: float
0018 |     std_target: float
0019 |     std_baseline: float
0020 |     cohen_d: float
0021 |     abs_cohen_d: float
0022 |     ks_stat: float
0023 |     ks_pvalue: float
0024 |     auc: float  # probability metric_target > metric_baseline
0025 |     direction: int  # +1 if target > baseline, -1 if baseline > target, 0 if tie-ish
0026 | 
0027 |     def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
0028 |         return asdict(self)
0029 | 
0030 | 
0031 | def _cohen_d(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray, eps: float = 1e-8) -> float:
0032 |     x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
0033 |     y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
0034 |     nx = x.size
0035 |     ny = y.size
0036 |     if nx < 2 or ny < 2:
0037 |         return 0.0
0038 |     mx = float(x.mean())
0039 |     my = float(y.mean())
0040 |     vx = float(x.var(ddof=1))
0041 |     vy = float(y.var(ddof=1))
0042 |     # pooled std
0043 |     sp2 = ((nx - 1) * vx + (ny - 1) * vy) / max(nx + ny - 2, 1)
0044 |     sp = math.sqrt(max(sp2, eps))
0045 |     return (mx - my) / sp
0046 | 
0047 | 
0048 | def _ks_2sample(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> Tuple[float, float]:
0049 |     """
0050 |     Tiny self-contained 2-sample KS test (approx p-value).
0051 | 
0052 |     We could use scipy.stats.ks_2samp, but this keeps the dependency surface small.
0053 |     This is not meant to be super-precise; it's just a "is there a big distribution gap?" flag.
0054 |     """
0055 |     x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
0056 |     y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
0057 |     if x.size == 0 or y.size == 0:
0058 |         return 0.0, 1.0
0059 | 
0060 |     # Empirical CDFs
0061 |     data_all = np.concatenate([x, y])
0062 |     data_sorted = np.sort(data_all)
0063 |     nx = x.size
0064 |     ny = y.size
0065 | 
0066 |     # ranks → CDF
0067 |     cdf_x = np.searchsorted(np.sort(x), data_sorted, side="right") / nx
0068 |     cdf_y = np.searchsorted(np.sort(y), data_sorted, side="right") / ny
0069 | 
0070 |     diffs = np.abs(cdf_x - cdf_y)
0071 |     d = float(diffs.max())
0072 | 
0073 |     # Rough asymptotic p-value (Smirnov)
0074 |     en = math.sqrt(nx * ny / (nx + ny))
0075 |     try:
0076 |         p = 2.0 * math.exp(-2.0 * (d * en) ** 2)
0077 |     except OverflowError:
0078 |         p = 0.0
0079 |     p = max(0.0, min(1.0, p))
0080 |     return d, p
0081 | 
0082 | 
0083 | def _auc_from_scores(x: np.ndarray, y: np.ndarray) -> float:
0084 |     """
0085 |     AUC-style probability that a random target > random baseline.
0086 |     Uses Mann–Whitney U on 1D feature only.
0087 | 
0088 |     Returns:
0089 |         auc \in [0,1], where 0.5 ~ no separation.
0090 |     """
0091 |     x = np.asarray(x, dtype=np.float64)
0092 |     y = np.asarray(y, dtype=np.float64)
0093 |     nx = x.size
0094 |     ny = y.size
0095 |     if nx == 0 or ny == 0:
0096 |         return 0.5
0097 | 
0098 |     # rank all values
0099 |     values = np.concatenate([x, y])
0100 |     ranks = values.argsort().argsort().astype(np.float64) + 1.0  # 1-based ranks
0101 |     r_x = ranks[:nx].sum()
0102 | 
0103 |     # Mann–Whitney U for x
0104 |     u_x = r_x - nx * (nx + 1) / 2.0
0105 |     auc = u_x / (nx * ny)
0106 |     return float(max(0.0, min(1.0, auc)))
0107 | 
0108 | 
0109 | def compute_metric_importance(
0110 |     X_target: np.ndarray,
0111 |     X_baseline: np.ndarray,
0112 |     metric_names: Sequence[str],
0113 |     *,
0114 |     top_k: int | None = None,
0115 |     min_effect: float = 0.0,
0116 | ) -> List[MetricImportance]:
0117 |     """
0118 |     GAP-style per-metric importance analysis.
0119 | 
0120 |     Args:
0121 |         X_target:   (N_t, D) matrix for "good" / targeted cohort
0122 |         X_baseline: (N_b, D) matrix for baseline / "bad" cohort
0123 |         metric_names: length-D list of names
0124 |         top_k:      optionally keep only top_k metrics by |Cohen's d|
0125 |         min_effect: optionally require |d| >= this threshold
0126 | 
0127 |     Returns:
0128 |         List[MetricImportance], sorted by abs_cohen_d descending.
0129 |     """
0130 |     Xt = np.asarray(X_target, dtype=np.float64)
0131 |     Xb = np.asarray(X_baseline, dtype=np.float64)
0132 |     metric_names = list(metric_names)
0133 | 
0134 |     if Xt.ndim != 2 or Xb.ndim != 2:
0135 |         raise ValueError(f"compute_metric_importance: expected 2D matrices, got {Xt.shape} and {Xb.shape}")
0136 |     if Xt.shape[1] != Xb.shape[1]:
0137 |         raise ValueError(f"compute_metric_importance: dim mismatch {Xt.shape[1]} vs {Xb.shape[1]}")
0138 |     if len(metric_names) != Xt.shape[1]:
0139 |         raise ValueError(
0140 |             f"metric_names length {len(metric_names)} != num_metrics {Xt.shape[1]}"
0141 |         )
0142 | 
0143 |     N_t, D = Xt.shape
0144 |     N_b, _ = Xb.shape
0145 |     if N_t == 0 or N_b == 0 or D == 0:
0146 |         return []
0147 | 
0148 |     out: List[MetricImportance] = []
0149 |     for j in range(D):
0150 |         name = metric_names[j]
0151 |         tcol = Xt[:, j]
0152 |         bcol = Xb[:, j]
0153 | 
0154 |         m_t = float(np.mean(tcol))
0155 |         m_b = float(np.mean(bcol))
0156 |         s_t = float(np.std(tcol))
0157 |         s_b = float(np.std(bcol))
0158 | 
0159 |         d = _cohen_d(tcol, bcol)
0160 |         ks_stat, ks_p = _ks_2sample(tcol, bcol)
0161 |         auc = _auc_from_scores(tcol, bcol)
0162 | 
0163 |         # direction: which way is "better"?
0164 |         if abs(d) < 1e-6:
0165 |             direction = 0
0166 |         else:
0167 |             direction = 1 if d > 0 else -1
0168 | 
0169 |         imp = MetricImportance(
0170 |             name=name,
0171 |             mean_target=m_t,
0172 |             mean_baseline=m_b,
0173 |             std_target=s_t,
0174 |             std_baseline=s_b,
0175 |             cohen_d=d,
0176 |             abs_cohen_d=abs(d),
0177 |             ks_stat=ks_stat,
0178 |             ks_pvalue=ks_p,
0179 |             auc=auc,
0180 |             direction=direction,
0181 |         )
0182 |         out.append(imp)
0183 | 
0184 |     # sort most discriminative first
0185 |     out.sort(key=lambda r: r.abs_cohen_d, reverse=True)
0186 | 
0187 |     # apply filters
0188 |     if min_effect > 0.0:
0189 |         out = [r for r in out if r.abs_cohen_d >= min_effect]
0190 |     if top_k is not None and top_k > 0:
0191 |         out = out[:top_k]
0192 | 
0193 |     return out
0194 |

0199 | ) -> Path:
0200 |     p = Path(path)

0203 |     with p.open("w", encoding="utf-8") as f:
0204 |         json.dump(payload, f, indent=2)

0321 |     def apply(

0422 |     # Internals
0423 |     # ------------------------------------------------------------------
0424 | 
0425 |     def _match_rule(
0426 |         self,
0427 |         rule: MetricMappingRule,
0428 |         metric_names: Sequence[str],
0429 |         name_to_idx: Dict[str, int],

0431 |         """

0458 | 
0459 |     def _normalize_columns(
0460 |         self,
0461 |         scores: np.ndarray,
0462 |         names: Sequence[str],
0463 |     ) -> np.ndarray:
0464 |         """
0465 |         Min–max normalize each column into [0, 1] according to rule.normalize

0467 |         """

0470 | 
0471 |         scores = scores.copy()
0472 |         col_count = scores.shape[1]
0473 | 
0474 |         log.info(
0475 |             "MetricMapper._normalize_columns: col_count=%d rules=%d normalize_unmatched=%r",
0476 |             col_count,
0477 |             len(self.rules),
0478 |             self.normalize_unmatched,
0479 |         )
0480 | 
0481 |         # Pre-build: name -> rule
0482 |         name_to_rule: Dict[str, MetricMappingRule] = {}
0483 |         for rule in self.rules:
0484 |             for name in names:
0485 |                 if rule.patterns and any(fnmatch(name, p) for p in rule.patterns):
0486 |                     name_to_rule[name] = rule

0488 |                     name_to_rule[name] = rule
0489 | 
0490 |         eps = 1e-8
0491 | 
0492 |         for j in range(col_count):
0493 |             col = scores[:, j]
0494 |             name = names[j]
0495 |             rule = name_to_rule.get(name)
0496 | 
0497 |             if rule is not None:

0500 |                         "MetricMapper._normalize_columns: skipping normalization for %r "

0509 |                         "(no rule, normalize_unmatched=False)",
0510 |                         name,
0511 |                     )
0512 |                     continue
0513 | 
0514 |             cmin = float(col.min())
0515 |             cmax = float(col.max())
0516 |             if cmax - cmin < eps:

0518 |                 log.info(
0519 |                     "MetricMapper._normalize_columns: %r is flat (min=max=%.4f); set to 0.5",
0520 |                     name,
0521 |                     cmin,
0522 |                 )

0524 |                 scores[:, j] = (col - cmin) / (cmax - cmin)
0525 |                 log.info(
0526 |                     "MetricMapper._normalize_columns: normalized %r from [%.4f, %.4f] to [0,1]",
0527 |                     name,
0528 |                     cmin,
0529 |                     cmax,
0530 |                 )

0540 |         return any(fnmatch(self._canon(p), n) or fnmatch(n, self._canon(p)) for p in patterns)

0075 |                         self._runs[run_id].append(name)

0077 |     def get_stable_core(
0078 |         self,
0079 |         min_runs: int = 5,
0080 |         stability_threshold: float = 0.6
0081 |     ) -> List[Tuple[str, float]]:
0082 |         """Find metrics that consistently distinguish good from bad reasoning"""
0083 |         if not self.enabled or not self._metrics:
0084 |             return []
0085 |             
0086 |         stable_metrics = []

0088 |         for metric_name, stats in self._metrics.items():
0089 |             # Only consider metrics that appeared in enough runs
0090 |             if metric_name not in self._runs or len(self._runs[metric_name]) < min_runs:

0095 |             total_runs = 0

0048 | class ScorableProcessor(ProgressMixin):
0049 |     """
0050 |     PURE PROCESSOR:
0051 |       - Applies feature modules (DomainFeature, NerFeature, EmbeddingFeature, MetricsFeature, VpmFeature, etc)
0052 |       - Builds a standardized ScorableRow via RowBuilder
0053 |       - Persists deltas through Writers
0054 |       - NO bus
0055 |       - NO manifest
0056 |       - NO hydration providers (hydration is a feature)
0057 |     """
0058 | 
0059 |     def __init__(self, cfg, memory, container, logger):
0060 |         self.cfg = cfg or {}
0061 |         self.memory = memory
0062 |         self.container = container
0063 |         self.logger = logger
0064 | 
0065 |         # ---------- Row features ----------
0066 |         feature_cfgs = self.cfg.get("feature_configs", {}) or {}
0067 |         self.features = []
0068 | 
0069 |         for name, subcfg in feature_cfgs.items():  # preserves YAML order
0070 |             cls = FEATURE_REGISTRY.get(name)
0071 |             if cls is None:
0072 |                 log.warning(f"[SP] unknown feature '{name}' ignored")
0073 |                 continue
0074 |             feat = cls(
0075 |                 cfg=subcfg or {},
0076 |                 memory=self.memory,
0077 |                 container=self.container,
0078 |                 logger=self.logger,
0079 |             )
0080 |             if getattr(feat, "enabled", True):
0081 |                 self.features.append(feat)
0082 |                 log.info(f"[SP] feature loaded: {name} → {cls.__name__}")
0083 |             else:
0084 |                 log.info(f"[SP] feature disabled: {name}")
0085 | 
0086 |         # ---------- Group features ----------
0087 |         self.group_features = []
0088 |         for name, subcfg in (
0089 |             self.cfg.get("group_feature_configs", {}) or {}
0090 |         ).items():
0091 |             cls = GROUP_FEATURE_REGISTRY.get(name)
0092 |             if not cls:
0093 |                 log.warning("[SP] unknown group feature '%s'", name)
0094 |                 continue
0095 |             gf = cls(  # MUST pass the sub-config
0096 |                 cfg=subcfg,  # ← not `cfg`
0097 |                 memory=self.memory,
0098 |                 container=self.container,
0099 |                 logger=self.logger,
0100 |             )
0101 |             if gf.enabled:
0102 |                 self.group_features.append(gf)
0103 |                 log.info(
0104 |                     "[SP] group feature loaded: %s → %s", name, cls.__name__
0105 |                 )
0106 | 
0107 |         # ---------- Row builder ----------
0108 |         self.row_builder = RowBuilder()
0109 | 
0110 |         # ---------- Writers (optional legacy) ----------
0111 |         self.writers = self.cfg.get(
0112 |             "writers", []
0113 |         )  # consider removing entirely later
0114 | 
0115 |         # ---------- Progress + misc ----------
0116 |         self._init_progress(self.container, self.logger)
0117 |         self.skip_if_exists = bool(self.cfg.get("skip_if_exists", True))
0118 | 
0119 |     # -----------------------------------------------------
0120 |     # Public API
0121 |     # -----------------------------------------------------
0122 | 
0123 |     async def process(
0124 |         self,
0125 |         input_data: Union[Scorable, Dict[str, Any]],
0126 |         context: Dict[str, Any],
0127 |     ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
0128 |         t0 = time.perf_counter()
0129 |         scorable = (
0130 |             input_data
0131 |             if isinstance(input_data, Scorable)
0132 |             else ScorableFactory.from_dict(input_data)
0133 |         )
0134 |         acc: Dict[str, Any] = {}
0135 | 
0136 |         for feature in self.features:
0137 |             try:
0138 |                 log.debug(
0139 |                     f"[ScorableProcessor] applying feature: {feature.name}"
0140 |                 )
0141 |                 acc = await feature.apply(scorable, acc, context)
0142 |                 log.debug(
0143 |                     f"[ScorableProcessor] applied feature: {feature.name}"
0144 |                 )
0145 |             except Exception as e:
0146 |                 log.warning(
0147 |                     f"[ScorableProcessor] Feature {feature.name} failed: {e}"
0148 |                 )
0149 | 
0150 |         row_obj = self.row_builder.build(scorable, acc)
0151 |         row = row_obj.to_dict()
0152 | 
0153 |         for writer in self.writers:
0154 |             try:
0155 |                 await writer.persist(scorable, acc)
0156 |             except Exception as e:
0157 |                 log.warning(
0158 |                     f"[ScorableProcessor] Writer {getattr(writer, 'name', 'writer')} failed: {e}"
0159 |                 )
0160 | 
0161 |         log.debug(
0162 |             "[ScorableProcessor] done id=%s in %.2f ms",
0163 |             scorable.id,
0164 |             (time.perf_counter() - t0) * 1000,
0165 |         )
0166 |         return row
0167 | 
0168 |     # -----------------------------------------------------
0169 |     # Batch processing
0170 |     # -----------------------------------------------------
0171 | 
0172 |     async def process_many(
0173 |         self,
0174 |         inputs: List[Union[Scorable, Dict[str, Any]]],
0175 |         context: Dict[str, Any],
0176 |     ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
0177 |         n = len(inputs)
0178 |         t_all = time.perf_counter()
0179 | 
0180 |         task_rows = (
0181 |             f"ScorableProcess:rows:{context.get(PIPELINE_RUN_ID, 'na')}"
0182 |         )
0183 |         self.pstart(task=task_rows, total=n)
0184 | 
0185 |         rows: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
0186 |         try:
0187 |             for idx, sc in enumerate(inputs):
0188 |                 row = await self.process(sc, context)
0189 |                 rows.append(row)
0190 |                 self.ptick(task=task_rows, done=idx + 1, total=n)
0191 |         finally:
0192 |             self.pdone(task=task_rows)
0193 | 
0194 |         # Optional: enforce simple dependencies if group features declare `requires`
0195 |         available = {
0196 |             getattr(f, "name", f"f{idx}")
0197 |             for idx, f in enumerate(self.group_features)
0198 |         }
0199 |         for gf in self.group_features:
0200 |             reqs = getattr(gf, "requires", []) or []
0201 |             missing = [r for r in reqs if r not in available]
0202 |             if missing:
0203 |                 log.warning(
0204 |                     f"[SP] group feature '{gf.name}' missing requirements: {missing}"
0205 |                 )
0206 | 
0207 |         task_group = (
0208 |             f"ScorableProcess:group:{context.get('pipeline_run_id', 'na')}"
0209 |         )
0210 |         self.pstart(task=task_group, total=len(self.group_features))
0211 |         try:
0212 |             for i, gf in enumerate(self.group_features, start=1):
0213 |                 try:
0214 |                     log.info(
0215 |                         f"[ScorableProcessor] applying group feature: {gf.name}"
0216 |                     )
0217 |                     rows = await gf.apply(rows, context)
0218 |                     log.info(
0219 |                         f"[ScorableProcessor] applied group feature: {gf.name}"
0220 |                     )
0221 |                 except Exception as e:
0222 |                     log.warning(
0223 |                         f"[ScorableProcessor] Group feature {gf.name} failed: {e}"
0224 |                     )
0225 |                 self.ptick(
0226 |                     task=task_group, done=i, total=len(self.group_features)
0227 |                 )
0228 |         finally:
0229 |             self.pdone(task=task_group)
0230 | 
0231 |         if context is not None:
0232 |             context.setdefault("feature_reports", self.feature_reports())
0233 | 
0234 |         log.debug(
0235 |             "[ScorableProcessor] batch_size=%d finished in %.2f ms",
0236 |             n,
0237 |             (time.perf_counter() - t_all) * 1000,
0238 |         )
0239 |         return rows
0240 | 
0241 |     def feature_reports(self) -> list[dict]:
0242 |         reps = []
0243 |         # per-row features
0244 |         for f in self.features:
0245 |             if hasattr(f, "report"):
0246 |                 try:
0247 |                     reps.append(_report_to_dict(f.report(), f))
0248 |                 except Exception as e:
0249 |                     reps.append(
0250 |                         {
0251 |                             "name": getattr(f, "name", f.__class__.__name__),
0252 |                             "kind": getattr(f, "kind", "row"),
0253 |                             "ok": False,
0254 |                             "summary": "report() raised",
0255 |                             "details": {"error": str(e)},
0256 |                         }
0257 |                     )
0258 |         # group features
0259 |         for gf in self.group_features:
0260 |             try:
0261 |                 reps.append(_report_to_dict(gf.report(), gf))
0262 |             except Exception as e:
0263 |                 reps.append(
0264 |                     {
0265 |                         "name": getattr(gf, "name", gf.__class__.__name__),
0266 |                         "kind": getattr(gf, "kind", "group"),
0267 |                         "ok": False,
0268 |                         "summary": "report() raised",
0269 |                         "details": {"error": str(e)},
0270 |                     }
0271 |                 )
0272 |         return reps
0273 | 
0274 | 
0275 | def _report_to_dict(rep, feature):
0276 |     # 1) FeatureReport dataclass → dict
0277 |     try:
0278 |         from stephanie.scoring.metrics.feature.feature_report import \
0279 |             FeatureReport  # adjust import if needed
0280 | 
0281 |         if isinstance(rep, FeatureReport):
0282 |             d = asdict(rep)
0283 |             # ensure minimal fields
0284 |             d.setdefault(
0285 |                 "name", getattr(feature, "name", feature.__class__.__name__)
0286 |             )
0287 |             d.setdefault("kind", getattr(feature, "kind", "row"))
0288 |             return d
0289 |     except Exception:
0290 |         pass
0291 | 
0292 |     # 2) Already a mapping → ensure name/kind
0293 |     if isinstance(rep, dict):
0294 |         rep = dict(rep)
0295 |         rep.setdefault(
0296 |             "name", getattr(feature, "name", feature.__class__.__name__)
0297 |         )
0298 |         rep.setdefault("kind", getattr(feature, "kind", "row"))
0299 |         rep.setdefault("ok", rep.get("ok", True))
0300 |         return rep
0301 | 
0302 |     # 3) Fallback: opaque value
0303 |     return {
0304 |         "name": getattr(feature, "name", feature.__class__.__name__),
0305 |         "kind": getattr(feature, "kind", "row"),
0306 |         "ok": False,
0307 |         "summary": "Unknown report type",
0308 |         "details": {"raw": repr(rep)},
0309 |         "warnings": ["non-dict/non-FeatureReport report"],
0310 |     }

0006 | 
0007 | from stephanie.scoring.metrics.feature.feature_report import FeatureReport
0008 | from stephanie.scoring.scorable import Scorable
0009 | 
0010 | 
0011 | class BaseFeature(abc.ABC):
0012 |     """
0013 |     A Feature transforms (scorable, acc, context) → updated acc.
0014 | 
0015 |     Rules:
0016 |     - NEVER mutate the `scorable` object.
0017 |     - ALWAYS return the updated accumulator dict.
0018 |     - Each feature is fully self-contained.
0019 |     - Features may depend on external tools/services (passed in __init__).
0020 |     """
0021 | 
0022 |     name: str = "base_feature"
0023 | 
0024 |     def __init__(self, cfg: dict, memory, container, logger):
0025 |         self.cfg = cfg or {}
0026 |         self.memory = memory
0027 |         self.container = container
0028 |         self.logger = logger
0029 | 
0030 |     @abc.abstractmethod
0031 |     async def apply(
0032 |         self,
0033 |         scorable: Scorable,
0034 |         acc: Dict[str, Any],
0035 |         context: Dict[str, Any],
0036 |     ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
0037 |         """
0038 |         Given a Scorable + current accumulator + pipeline context,
0039 |         compute new attributes and return updated accumulator.
0040 |         """
0041 |         raise NotImplementedError
0042 | 
0043 |     def report(self) -> FeatureReport:
0044 |         # default no-op
0045 |         return FeatureReport(name=self.name, kind="row", ok=True, summary="no-op")
