```python
0002 | from __future__ import annotations
0003 | 
0004 | from dataclasses import dataclass
0005 | from datetime import datetime
0006 | from typing import Dict, List, Optional
0007 | 
0008 | from stephanie.constants import GOAL
0009 | from stephanie.data.score_bundle import ScoreBundle
0010 | from stephanie.scoring.scorable import Scorable
0011 | from stephanie.scoring.scorer.base_scorer import BaseScorer
0012 | 
0013 | 
0014 | @dataclass
0015 | class ScoreAttempt:
0016 |     scorer_name: str
0017 |     success: bool
0018 |     error: Optional[str] = None
0019 |     score_bundle: Optional[ScoreBundle] = None
0020 |     timestamp: datetime = datetime.now()
0021 | 
0022 | 
0023 | class FallbackScorer(BaseScorer):
0024 |     """
0025 |     A composite scorer that tries multiple scorers in order of preference.
0026 |     Falls back when a scorer fails due to missing model, data, or timeout.
0027 |     """
0028 | 
0029 |     def __init__(
0030 |         self,
0031 |         cfg,
0032 |         memory,
0033 |         logger,
0034 |         scorers: List[BaseScorer],
0035 |         fallback_order: Optional[List[str]] = None,
0036 |         default_fallback: str = "llm",
0037 |     ): 
0038 |         """
0039 |         Args:
0040 |             scorers: List of scorers to try
0041 |             fallback_order: Order of scorer preference (e.g. ["svm", "mrq", "llm"])
0042 |             default_fallback: Final fallback if all scorers fail
0043 |             logger: Optional logger
0044 |         """
0045 |         super().__init__(cfg=cfg, memory=memory, logger=logger)
0046 |         self.scorers = {scorer.name: scorer for scorer in scorers}
0047 |         self.fallback_order = fallback_order or list(self.scorers.keys())
0048 |         self.default_fallback = default_fallback
0049 | 
0050 |     def _score_core(self, context: dict, scorable: Scorable, dimensions: List[str] = None) -> ScoreBundle:
0051 |         """
0052 |         Try scorers in order. Returns first successful score bundle.
0053 |         If all fail, returns neutral score with fallback reason.
0054 |         """
0055 |         goal = context.get(GOAL, {})
0056 |         scorer_used = None
0057 |         attempts = []
0058 | 
0059 |         for scorer_name in self.fallback_order:
0060 |             scorer = self.scorers.get(scorer_name)
0061 | 
0062 |             if not scorer:
0063 |                 self.logger.log(
0064 |                     "ScorerNotRegistered",
0065 |                     {"scorer_name": scorer_name, "available_scorers": list(self.scorers.keys())}
0066 |                 )
0067 |                 continue
0068 | 
0069 |             try:
0070 |                 self.logger.log("TryingScorer", {"scorer": scorer_name, "target": scorable.id})
0071 |                 score_bundle = scorer.score(context, scorable, dimensions=dimensions)
0072 | 
0073 |                 if score_bundle.is_valid():
0074 |                     scorer_used = scorer_name
0075 |                     attempts.append(ScoreAttempt(
0076 |                         scorer_name=scorer_name,
0077 |                         success=True,
0078 |                         score_bundle=score_bundle
0079 |                     ))
0080 |                     self.logger.log(
0081 |                         "ScoreSuccess",
0082 |                         {"scorer": scorer_name, "target": scorable.id, "scores": score_bundle.to_dict()}
0083 |                     )
0084 |                     break
0085 |                 else:
0086 |                     attempts.append(ScoreAttempt(
0087 |                         scorer_name=scorer_name,
0088 |                         success=False,
0089 |                         error="Invalid score bundle"
0090 |                     ))
0091 |                     self.logger.log(
0092 |                         "ScoreInvalid",
0093 |                         {"scorer": scorer_name, "target": scorable.id}
0094 |                     )
0095 | 
0096 |             except Exception as e:
0097 |                 attempts.append(ScoreAttempt(
0098 |                     scorer_name=scorer_name,
0099 |                     success=False,
0100 |                     error=str(e)
0101 |                 ))
0102 |                 self.logger.log(
0103 |                     "ScoreFailed",
0104 |                     {"scorer": scorer_name, "target": scorable.id, "error": str(e)}
0105 |                 )
0106 |                 continue
0107 | 
0108 |         if scorer_used:
0109 |             return score_bundle
0110 | 
0111 |         # Final fallback: use default scorer
0112 |         default_scorer = self.scorers.get(self.default_fallback)
0113 |         if default_scorer:
0114 |             self.logger.log(
0115 |                 "FinalFallbackUsed",
0116 |                 {"scorer": self.default_fallback, "target": scorable.id}
0117 |             )
0118 |             return default_scorer.score(context, scorable, dimensions=dimensions)
0119 | 
0120 |         # If even fallback fails, return neutral score
0121 |         self.logger.log(
0122 |             "AllScorersFailed",
0123 |             {"target": scorable.id, "attempts": [a.scorer_name for a in attempts]}
0124 |         )
0125 |         return ScoreBundle.from_dict({
0126 |             dim: 0.5 for dim in dimensions or ["usefulness", "novelty", "alignment"]
0127 |         })
0128 | 
0129 |     def load_models(self):
0130 |         """Load models for all scorers."""
0131 |         for scorer in self.scorers.values():
0132 |             try:
0133 |                 scorer.load_models()
0134 |             except Exception as e:
0135 |                 self.logger.log("ModelLoadFailed", {"scorer": scorer.name, "error": str(e)})
0136 | 
0137 |     def train(self, samples_by_dim: Dict[str, list]):
0138 |         """Train all scorers that support training."""
0139 |         for scorer in self.scorers.values():
0140 |             try:
0141 |                 scorer.train(samples_by_dim)
0142 |             except Exception as e:
0143 |                 self.logger.log("TrainingFailed", {"scorer": scorer.name, "error": str(e)})
0144 | 
0145 |     def save_models(self):
0146 |         """Save models for all scorers."""
0147 |         for scorer in self.scorers.values():
0148 |             try:
0149 |                 scorer.save_models()
0150 |             except Exception as e:
0151 |                 self.logger.log("ModelSaveFailed", {"scorer": scorer.name, "error": str(e)})
```

```python
0001 | # stephanie/scoring/hallucination/hallucination_scorer.py
0002 | 
0003 | from __future__ import annotations
0004 | 
0005 | import logging
0006 | from typing import Any, Dict, List
0007 | 
0008 | import numpy as np
0009 | 
0010 | from stephanie.data.score_bundle import ScoreBundle
0011 | from stephanie.data.score_result import ScoreResult
0012 | from stephanie.scoring.scorable import Scorable
0013 | from stephanie.scoring.scorer.base_scorer import BaseScorer
0014 | 
0015 | log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
0016 | 
0017 | 
0018 | class HallucinationScorer(BaseScorer):
0019 |     """
0020 |     Geometric Hallucination Energy scorer.
0021 | 
0022 |     Computes projection residual of response embedding onto
0023 |     span of historical/context embeddings.
0024 | 
0025 |     Lower score = better grounding.
0026 |     """
0027 | 
0028 |     def __init__(self, cfg, memory, container, logger):
0029 |         super().__init__(cfg, memory, container, logger)
0030 | 
0031 |         self.model_type = "hallucination"
0032 |         self.dimension_name = cfg.get(
0033 |             "dimension_name", "hallucination_energy"
0034 |         )
0035 | 
0036 |         # Optional rank truncation for SVD
0037 |         self.max_rank = int(cfg.get("max_rank", 32))
0038 |         self.eps = float(cfg.get("eps", 1e-8))
0039 | 
0040 |     # ---------------------------------------------------------
0041 |     # Core scoring logic
0042 |     # ---------------------------------------------------------
0043 |     def _score_core(
0044 |         self,
0045 |         context: Dict[str, Any],
0046 |         scorable: Scorable,
0047 |         dimensions: List[str],
0048 |     ) -> ScoreBundle:
0049 | 
0050 |         # Only compute if requested
0051 |         if self.dimension_name not in dimensions:
0052 |             return ScoreBundle(results={})
0053 | 
0054 |         # -----------------------------------------------------
0055 |         # 1️⃣ Get response embedding
0056 |         # -----------------------------------------------------
0057 |         resp_vec = np.asarray(
0058 |             self.memory.embedding.get_or_create(scorable.text),
0059 |             dtype=np.float32,
0060 |         )
0061 | 
0062 |         if np.linalg.norm(resp_vec) < self.eps:
0063 |             score = 1.0  # Degenerate embedding → treat as maximal energy
0064 |             return self._build_bundle(score, resp_vec, [], rank=0)
0065 | 
0066 |         # -----------------------------------------------------
0067 |         # 2️⃣ Build evidence/history matrix
0068 |         # -----------------------------------------------------
0069 |         history_texts = self._extract_history(context)
0070 | 
0071 |         history_vecs = []
0072 |         for txt in history_texts:
0073 |             try:
0074 |                 vec = np.asarray(
0075 |                     self.memory.embedding.get_or_create(txt),
0076 |                     dtype=np.float32,
0077 |                 )
0078 |                 if np.linalg.norm(vec) > self.eps:
0079 |                     history_vecs.append(vec)
0080 |             except Exception:
0081 |                 continue
0082 | 
0083 |         if not history_vecs:
0084 |             # No grounding reference → maximal energy
0085 |             score = 1.0
0086 |             return self._build_bundle(score, resp_vec, [], rank=0)
0087 | 
0088 |         E = np.stack(history_vecs, axis=0)
0089 | 
0090 |         # -----------------------------------------------------
0091 |         # 3️⃣ Compute orthonormal basis via truncated SVD
0092 |         # -----------------------------------------------------
0093 |         try:
0094 |             U, S, Vt = np.linalg.svd(E, full_matrices=False)
0095 |             rank = min(self.max_rank, U.shape[1])
0096 |             U_r = U[:, :rank]
0097 |         except np.linalg.LinAlgError:
0098 |             score = 1.0
0099 |             return self._build_bundle(score, resp_vec, history_vecs, rank=0)
0100 | 
0101 |         # -----------------------------------------------------
0102 |         # 4️⃣ Projection
0103 |         # -----------------------------------------------------
0104 |         projection = U_r @ (U_r.T @ resp_vec)
0105 |         residual_vec = resp_vec - projection
0106 | 
0107 |         residual_norm = float(np.linalg.norm(residual_vec))
0108 |         resp_norm = float(np.linalg.norm(resp_vec))
0109 | 
0110 |         score = residual_norm / (resp_norm + self.eps)
0111 | 
0112 |         # Clip for safety
0113 |         score = float(np.clip(score, 0.0, 1.0))
0114 | 
0115 |         return self._build_bundle(
0116 |             score,
0117 |             resp_vec,
0118 |             history_vecs,
0119 |             rank=rank,
0120 |             residual_norm=residual_norm,
0121 |             resp_norm=resp_norm,
0122 |         )
0123 | 
0124 |     # ---------------------------------------------------------
0125 |     # Helpers
0126 |     # ---------------------------------------------------------
0127 |     def _extract_history(self, context: Dict[str, Any]) -> List[str]:
0128 |         """
0129 |         Extract conversation history texts for grounding.
0130 |         Customize based on your context structure.
0131 |         """
0132 | 
0133 |         history = []
0134 | 
0135 |         # Common pattern: context["history"] = list of messages
0136 |         messages = context.get("history", [])
0137 | 
0138 |         for msg in messages:
0139 |             text = msg.get("text") if isinstance(msg, dict) else None
0140 |             if text:
0141 |                 history.append(text)
0142 | 
0143 |         # Also include goal text if present
0144 |         goal = context.get("goal", {})
0145 |         goal_text = goal.get("goal_text")
0146 |         if goal_text:
0147 |             history.append(goal_text)
0148 | 
0149 |         return history
0150 | 
0151 |     def _build_bundle(
0152 |         self,
0153 |         score: float,
0154 |         resp_vec: np.ndarray,
0155 |         history_vecs: List[np.ndarray],
0156 |         rank: int,
0157 |         residual_norm: float | None = None,
0158 |         resp_norm: float | None = None,
0159 |     ) -> ScoreBundle:
0160 | 
0161 |         attributes = {
0162 |             "history_count": len(history_vecs),
0163 |             "rank": rank,
0164 |         }
0165 | 
0166 |         if residual_norm is not None:
0167 |             attributes["residual_norm"] = residual_norm
0168 | 
0169 |         if resp_norm is not None:
0170 |             attributes["response_norm"] = resp_norm
0171 | 
0172 |         result = ScoreResult(
0173 |             dimension=self.dimension_name,
0174 |             score=score,
0175 |             rationale=f"Projection residual energy={round(score, 4)}",
0176 |             weight=1.0,
0177 |             source=self.model_type,
0178 |             attributes=attributes,
0179 |         )
0180 | 
0181 |         return ScoreBundle(results={self.dimension_name: result})
```

```python
0001 | # stephanie/scoring/scorer/hf_scorer.py
0002 | """
0003 | HuggingFace Scorer Module
0004 | 
0005 | A stable, production-ready scorer for HuggingFace Causal Language Models that computes
0006 | quality metrics through teacher-forced likelihood estimation. This scorer provides
0007 | foundational metrics that can be enhanced by plugins for SCM, calibration, and other
0008 | advanced features.
0009 | 
0010 | Key Features:
0011 | - Stable teacher-forced likelihood computation for response quality assessment
0012 | - Multiple quality dimensions: reasoning, knowledge, clarity, faithfulness, coverage
0013 | - Windows-friendly operation with eager attention fallback
0014 | - Memory-efficient inference with automatic device management
0015 | - Plugin architecture for extensible metric computation
0016 | - Comprehensive logging and error handling
0017 | 
0018 | The scorer computes basic statistics including:
0019 | - Perplexity (PPL) and mean log probability
0020 | - Token-level entropy and sequence length metrics
0021 | - Bits-per-byte (BPB) for information-theoretic analysis
0022 | - Token distribution analysis for interpretability
0023 | 
0024 | """
0025 | 
0026 | from __future__ import annotations
0027 | 
0028 | import gc
0029 | import logging
0030 | import math
0031 | import os
0032 | from typing import Any, Dict, List, Optional
0033 | 
0034 | import torch
0035 | import torch.nn.functional as F
0036 | from transformers import AutoModelForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer
0037 | 
0038 | from stephanie.constants import GOAL, GOAL_TEXT
0039 | from stephanie.data.score_bundle import ScoreBundle
0040 | from stephanie.data.score_result import ScoreResult
0041 | from stephanie.scoring.scorer.base_scorer import BaseScorer
0042 | 
0043 | # Module-level logger for comprehensive debugging and monitoring
0044 | log = logging.getLogger(__name__)
0045 | 
0046 | 
0047 | class HuggingFaceScorer(BaseScorer):
0048 |     """
0049 |     Simple, stable HF CausalLM scorer (Windows-friendly).
0050 |     
0051 |     This scorer computes teacher-forced likelihood statistics of responses conditioned
0052 |     on goals, providing foundational metrics for quality assessment. It serves as a
0053 |     base for plugin enhancements that add SCM, calibration, and other advanced features.
0054 |     
0055 |     Key Characteristics:
0056 |     - Computes: log probability, perplexity, entropy, length metrics, bits-per-byte
0057 |     - Does NOT compute: SCM or calibration (handled by plugins)
0058 |     - Stable operation: Uses eager attention to avoid Flash/SDPA issues
0059 |     - Memory efficient: Automatic device mapping and dtype selection
0060 |     - Extensible: Plugin architecture for additional metric computation
0061 |     
0062 |     The scorer processes text pairs (goal, response) and returns comprehensive
0063 |     statistical metrics that correlate with various quality dimensions.
0064 | 
0065 |     Attributes:
0066 |         model_type: Identifier for scorer type ("hf")
0067 |         model_name: HuggingFace model identifier or path
0068 |         tokenizer_name: Tokenizer identifier (defaults to model_name)
0069 |         max_seq_len: Maximum sequence length for processing
0070 |         device_map: HF device mapping strategy ("auto", "cuda", "cpu", etc.)
0071 |         trust_remote_code: Whether to trust remote code in model loading
0072 |         model_alias: Short alias for model in metric naming
0073 |         dimensions: List of quality dimensions to score
0074 |         cache_dir: Directory for model cache (falls back to HF_HOME)
0075 |         local_files_only: Whether to use only local model files
0076 |         torch_dtype: PyTorch data type for model (auto, float16, float32)
0077 |     """
0078 | 
0079 |     def __init__(self, cfg, memory, container, logger):
0080 |         """Initialize HuggingFaceScorer with configuration and dependencies."""
0081 |         super().__init__(cfg, memory, container, logger, enable_plugins=True)
0082 |         log.debug("Initializing HuggingFaceScorer with config: %s", 
0083 |                      {k: v for k, v in cfg.items() if not k.startswith('_')})
0084 |         
0085 |         self.model_type = "hf"
0086 | 
0087 |         # --- Configuration extraction with safe defaults ---
0088 |         self.model_name = str(cfg.get("model_name", "TinyLlama/TinyLlama-1.1B-Chat-v1.0"))
0089 |         self.tokenizer_name = cfg.get("tokenizer_name") or self.model_name
0090 |         self.max_seq_len = int(cfg.get("max_seq_len", 4096))
0091 |         self.device_map = cfg.get("device_map", "auto")
0092 |         self.trust_remote_code = bool(cfg.get("trust_remote_code", True))
0093 |         self.model_alias = str(cfg.get("model_alias", "hf"))
0094 |         self.dimensions: List[str] = cfg.get(
0095 |             "dimensions",
0096 |             ["reasoning", "knowledge", "clarity", "faithfulness", "coverage"],
0097 |         )
0098 |         log.debug("Model config: name=%s, tokenizer=%s, max_seq_len=%d", 
0099 |                      self.model_name, self.tokenizer_name, self.max_seq_len)
0100 | 
0101 |         # Optional HF cache configuration
0102 |         self.cache_dir = cfg.get("cache_dir") or os.environ.get("HF_HOME") or None
0103 |         self.local_files_only = bool(cfg.get("local_files_only", False))
0104 |         log.debug("Cache config: cache_dir=%s, local_files_only=%s", 
0105 |                      self.cache_dir, self.local_files_only)
0106 | 
0107 |         # Data type configuration for performance/memory tradeoffs
0108 |         dtype_str = str(cfg.get("torch_dtype", "auto"))
0109 |         if dtype_str == "auto":
0110 |             self.torch_dtype = torch.float16 if torch.cuda.is_available() else torch.float32
0111 |         else:
0112 |             self.torch_dtype = getattr(torch, dtype_str, torch.float32)
0113 |         log.debug("Data type: %s (from config: %s)", self.torch_dtype, dtype_str)
0114 | 
0115 |         # --- Tokenizer initialization with fallback strategy ---
0116 |         log.info("Loading tokenizer: %s", self.tokenizer_name)
0117 |         tok_id = self.tokenizer_name
0118 |         try:
0119 |             # First attempt: fast tokenizer for better performance
0120 |             self.tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
0121 |                 tok_id,
0122 |                 use_fast=True,
0123 |                 trust_remote_code=self.trust_remote_code,
0124 |                 cache_dir=self.cache_dir,
0125 |                 local_files_only=self.local_files_only,
0126 |             )
0127 |             log.debug("Fast tokenizer loaded successfully")
0128 |         except Exception as e_fast:
0129 |             # Fallback: slow tokenizer for compatibility
0130 |             log.warning("Fast tokenizer failed, falling back to slow tokenizer: %s", str(e_fast))
0131 |             self.tok = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(
0132 |                 tok_id,
0133 |                 use_fast=False,
0134 |                 trust_remote_code=self.trust_remote_code,
0135 |                 cache_dir=self.cache_dir,
0136 |                 local_files_only=self.local_files_only,
0137 |             )
0138 |             log.debug("Slow tokenizer loaded as fallback")
0139 | 
0140 |         # Ensure pad token is set for stable batch processing
0141 |         if not getattr(self.tok, "pad_token", None):
0142 |             try:
0143 |                 self.tok.pad_token = self.tok.eos_token
0144 |                 log.debug("Set pad_token to eos_token")
0145 |             except Exception as e:
0146 |                 log.warning("Failed to set pad_token: %s", str(e))
0147 | 
0148 |         # --- Model initialization with stability enhancements ---
0149 |         log.info("Loading model: %s", self.model_name)
0150 |         self.model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
0151 |             self.model_name,
0152 |             device_map=self.device_map,
0153 |             torch_dtype=self.torch_dtype,
0154 |             trust_remote_code=self.trust_remote_code,
0155 |             low_cpu_mem_usage=True,
0156 |             cache_dir=self.cache_dir,
0157 |             local_files_only=self.local_files_only,
0158 |         )
0159 |         self.model.eval()  # Set to evaluation mode
0160 |         log.debug("Model loaded and set to evaluation mode")
0161 | 
0162 |         # Force eager attention for stability (avoid SDPA/Flash issues on Windows/CUDA)
0163 |         try:
0164 |             if hasattr(self.model, "config"):
0165 |                 if getattr(self.model.config, "attn_implementation", None) is not None:
0166 |                     self.model.config.attn_implementation = "eager"
0167 |                     log.debug("Forced eager attention implementation")
0168 |                 setattr(self.model.config, "_attn_implementation", "eager")
0169 |         except Exception as e:
0170 |             log.debug("Could not force eager attention: %s", str(e))
0171 | 
0172 |         # For uniformity with other scorers in the system
0173 |         self.embedding_type = self.memory.embedding.name
0174 | 
0175 |         # Device detection for logging and monitoring
0176 |         try:
0177 |             p = next(self.model.parameters())
0178 |             dev_str = str(p.device)
0179 |         except Exception:
0180 |             dev_str = "unknown"
0181 |         log.debug("Model loaded on device: %s", dev_str)
0182 | 
0183 |         # Log successful initialization
0184 |         if self.logger:
0185 |             self.logger.log(
0186 |                 "HFScorerLoaded",
0187 |                 {
0188 |                     "model": self.model_name, 
0189 |                     "alias": self.model_alias, 
0190 |                     "device": dev_str, 
0191 |                     "dtype": str(self.torch_dtype)
0192 |                 },
0193 |             )
0194 |         log.info("HuggingFaceScorer initialized successfully: %s on %s", self.model_name, dev_str)
0195 | 
0196 |     # -----------------------------
0197 |     # Core Scoring Method
0198 |     # -----------------------------
0199 | 
0200 |     def _score_core(self, context: dict, scorable, dimensions: List[str]) -> ScoreBundle:
0201 |         """
0202 |         Core scoring method that computes basic language model statistics.
0203 |         
0204 |         This method computes teacher-forced likelihood metrics for a response
0205 |         conditioned on a goal context. The computed statistics serve as foundational
0206 |         metrics that can be enhanced by plugins for more sophisticated scoring.
0207 |         
0208 |         Args:
0209 |             context: Dictionary containing context information with GOAL/GOAL_TEXT
0210 |             scorable: Object containing the text response to be scored
0211 |             dimensions: List of quality dimensions to compute scores for
0212 |             
0213 |         Returns:
0214 |             ScoreBundle containing ScoreResult objects for each dimension with:
0215 |             - Basic statistics: perplexity, entropy, log probability, length metrics
0216 |             - Placeholder score (0.0) that can be enhanced by plugins
0217 |             - Comprehensive attributes for plugin processing
0218 |             - Rationale explaining the computed metrics
0219 |             
0220 |         Note:
0221 |             This method does NOT compute semantic scores - plugins are expected
0222 |             to enhance the results with SCM, calibration, and other advanced features.
0223 |         """
0224 |         log.debug("Starting core scoring for %d dimensions: %s", len(dimensions), dimensions)
0225 |         
0226 |         # Extract goal and response text from inputs
0227 |         goal_text = (context.get(GOAL, {}) or {}).get(GOAL_TEXT, "") or ""
0228 |         resp_text = scorable.text or ""
0229 |         log.debug("Scoring: goal=%d chars, response=%d chars", len(goal_text), len(resp_text))
0230 | 
0231 |         # Compute language model statistics with teacher forcing
0232 |         with torch.no_grad():
0233 |             stats = self._ll_stats(goal_text, resp_text)
0234 |         log.debug("LL stats computed: ppl=%.2f, mean_logprob=%.3f, entropy=%.3f", 
0235 |                      stats["ppl"], stats["mean_logprob"], stats["entropy_mean"])
0236 | 
0237 |         # Minimal attribute set that plugins can build upon
0238 |         base_attrs = {
0239 |             "mean_logprob": stats["mean_logprob"],    # Average log probability per token
0240 |             "ppl": stats["ppl"],                      # Perplexity (exp(-mean_logprob))
0241 |             "entropy_mean": stats["entropy_mean"],    # Average token-level entropy
0242 |             "len_tokens": stats["len_tokens"],        # Response length in tokens
0243 |             "len_chars": stats["len_chars"],          # Response length in characters
0244 |             "bytes_len": stats["bytes_len"],          # Response length in bytes
0245 |             "sum_nll_nats": stats["sum_nll_nats"],    # Total negative log likelihood
0246 |             "bpb": stats["bpb"],                      # Bits per byte (information density)
0247 |         }
0248 | 
0249 |         # Build feature vector for machine learning compatibility
0250 |         vector = self._build_base_vector(self.model_alias, base_attrs)
0251 |         log.debug("Base vector built with %d features", len(vector.get("columns", [])))
0252 | 
0253 |         # Create ScoreResult objects for each dimension
0254 |         results: Dict[str, ScoreResult] = {}
0255 |         for dim in dimensions:
0256 |             # Note: score=0.0 is a placeholder - plugins should set meaningful scores
0257 |             # The rationale provides human-readable explanation of the computed metrics
0258 |             results[dim] = ScoreResult(
0259 |                 dimension=dim,
0260 |                 score=0.0,  # Placeholder for plugin enhancement
0261 |                 source=self.model_type,
0262 |                 rationale=(
0263 |                     f"{self.model_alias}[{dim}] ppl={stats['ppl']:.2f}, "
0264 |                     f"H̄={stats['entropy_mean']:.3f}, lp̄={stats['mean_logprob']:.3f}"
0265 |                 ),
0266 |                 weight=1.0,
0267 |                 attributes={**base_attrs, **vector},  # Combine base stats with vector representation
0268 |             )
0269 |             log.debug("Created result for dimension '%s'", dim)
0270 | 
0271 |         log.info("Core scoring completed: %d results with ppl=%.2f", len(results), stats["ppl"])
0272 |         return ScoreBundle(results=results)
0273 | 
0274 |     # -----------------------------
0275 |     # Token Distribution Analysis
0276 |     # -----------------------------
0277 | 
0278 |     @torch.no_grad()
0279 |     def token_topk(self, goal: str, resp: str, k: int = 5) -> Optional[List[List[tuple[str, float]]]]:
0280 |         """
0281 |         Compute top-k token distributions for analysis and interpretability.
0282 |         
0283 |         This method provides detailed token-level probability distributions
0284 |         that can be used for:
0285 |         - Model behavior analysis and debugging
0286 |         - Confidence estimation and uncertainty quantification
0287 |         - Interpretability and explainability features
0288 |         
0289 |         Args:
0290 |             goal: Context/goal text that conditions the generation
0291 |             resp: Response text to analyze token distributions for
0292 |             k: Number of top tokens to return for each position
0293 |             
0294 |         Returns:
0295 |             List of token distributions for each response token position, where
0296 |             each distribution is a list of (token, probability) tuples, or
0297 |             None if k <= 0 or analysis is disabled
0298 |             
0299 |         Example:
0300 |             token_topk("What is AI?", "Artificial Intelligence", k=2)
0301 |             → [[("Artificial", 0.8), ("AI", 0.15)], [("Intelligence", 0.7), ("AI", 0.2)]]
0302 |         """
0303 |         if not k or k <= 0:
0304 |             log.debug("Token top-k analysis disabled (k=%d)", k)
0305 |             return None
0306 | 
0307 |         log.debug("Computing top-%d token distributions: goal=%d chars, resp=%d chars", 
0308 |                      k, len(goal), len(resp))
0309 |         
0310 |         try:
0311 |             # Tokenize inputs separately for precise position tracking
0312 |             enc_goal = self.tok(goal, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False)
0313 |             enc_resp = self.tok(resp, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False)
0314 |             
0315 |             # Combine goal and response for full context processing
0316 |             input_ids = torch.cat([enc_goal["input_ids"], enc_resp["input_ids"]], dim=1)
0317 |             input_ids = input_ids.to(self.model.device)
0318 |             attention_mask = torch.ones_like(input_ids)
0319 |             log.debug("Input sequence: %d tokens (goal: %d, resp: %d)", 
0320 |                          input_ids.shape[1], enc_goal["input_ids"].shape[1], enc_resp["input_ids"].shape[1])
0321 | 
0322 |             # Forward pass to get logits
0323 |             out = self.model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask, use_cache=False)
0324 |             shift_logits = out.logits[:, :-1, :]  # Shift for teacher forcing
0325 |             shift_labels = input_ids[:, 1:]
0326 |             
0327 |             # Extract response portion (after goal context)
0328 |             start = enc_goal["input_ids"].shape[1]
0329 |             resp_logits = shift_logits[:, start:, :]  # [1, Lr, V]
0330 |             probs = torch.softmax(resp_logits, dim=-1)[0]  # [Lr, V]
0331 |             log.debug("Response logits shape: %s, probs shape: %s", 
0332 |                          resp_logits.shape, probs.shape)
0333 | 
0334 |             # Compute top-k tokens and probabilities
0335 |             topv, topi = probs.topk(k, dim=-1)  # [Lr, k]
0336 |             toks = [self.tok.convert_ids_to_tokens(ids.tolist()) for ids in topi]
0337 |             
0338 |             # Format results as (token, probability) pairs
0339 |             result = [
0340 |                 [(toks[t][j], float(topv[t, j].item())) for j in range(k)]
0341 |                 for t in range(topi.size(0))
0342 |             ]
0343 |             log.debug("Computed top-%d distributions for %d response tokens", k, len(result))
0344 |             return result
0345 |             
0346 |         except Exception as e:
0347 |             log.error("Failed to compute token top-k: %s", str(e))
0348 |             return None
0349 | 
0350 |     # -----------------------------
0351 |     # Core Language Model Statistics
0352 |     # -----------------------------
0353 | 
0354 |     @torch.no_grad()
0355 |     def _ll_stats(self, goal: str, resp: str) -> Dict[str, float]:
0356 |         """
0357 |         Compute teacher-forced language model statistics for response given goal.
0358 |         
0359 |         This is the core method that computes all foundational metrics through
0360 |         teacher-forced likelihood estimation. It handles sequence length constraints
0361 |         through safe truncation and provides comprehensive statistical analysis.
0362 |         
0363 |         Args:
0364 |             goal: Context/goal text that conditions the generation
0365 |             resp: Response text to compute statistics for
0366 |             
0367 |         Returns:
0368 |             Dictionary containing:
0369 |             - mean_logprob: Average log probability per response token
0370 |             - ppl: Perplexity (exponential of negative mean log probability)
0371 |             - entropy_mean: Average token-level entropy in nats
0372 |             - len_tokens: Response length in tokens
0373 |             - len_chars: Response length in characters  
0374 |             - bytes_len: Response length in UTF-8 bytes
0375 |             - sum_nll_nats: Total negative log likelihood in nats
0376 |             - bpb: Bits per byte (information-theoretic measure)
0377 |             
0378 |         Note:
0379 |             Returns safe defaults for empty responses to avoid division by zero
0380 |         """
0381 |         log.debug("Computing LL stats: goal=%d chars, resp=%d chars", len(goal), len(resp))
0382 |         
0383 |         # Tokenize inputs separately for precise position tracking
0384 |         enc_goal = self.tok(goal, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False)
0385 |         enc_resp = self.tok(resp, return_tensors="pt", add_special_tokens=False)
0386 | 
0387 |         g_ids = enc_goal["input_ids"]
0388 |         r_ids = enc_resp["input_ids"]
0389 |         goal_len = g_ids.shape[1]
0390 |         total_len = goal_len + r_ids.shape[1]
0391 |         log.debug("Tokenized: goal=%d tokens, resp=%d tokens, total=%d", 
0392 |                      goal_len, r_ids.shape[1], total_len)
0393 | 
0394 |         # Combine goal and response tokens
0395 |         input_ids = torch.cat([g_ids, r_ids], dim=1)
0396 |         attention_mask = torch.ones_like(input_ids)
0397 | 
0398 |         # Handle sequence length constraints with safe truncation
0399 |         if total_len > self.max_seq_len:
0400 |             cut = total_len - self.max_seq_len
0401 |             input_ids = input_ids[:, cut:]
0402 |             attention_mask = attention_mask[:, cut:]
0403 |             resp_start = max(0, goal_len - cut)
0404 |             log.debug("Sequence truncated: cut=%d tokens, new_total=%d, resp_start=%d", 
0405 |                          cut, input_ids.shape[1], resp_start)
0406 |         else:
0407 |             resp_start = goal_len
0408 |             log.debug("No truncation needed, resp_start=%d", resp_start)
0409 | 
0410 |         # Move to model device for inference
0411 |         device = next(self.model.parameters()).device
0412 |         input_ids = input_ids.to(device)
0413 |         attention_mask = attention_mask.to(device)
0414 |         log.debug("Moved inputs to device: %s", device)
0415 | 
0416 |         # Forward pass to compute logits
0417 |         out = self.model(input_ids=input_ids, attention_mask=attention_mask, use_cache=False)
0418 |         logits = out.logits  # [B, T, V]
0419 |         log.debug("Model forward completed: logits shape=%s", logits.shape)
0420 | 
0421 |         # Shift for teacher-forcing alignment
0422 |         shift_logits = logits[:, :-1, :]    # Predict next token
0423 |         shift_labels = input_ids[:, 1:]     # Actual next token
0424 | 
0425 |         # Extract response portion after goal context
0426 |         resp_logits = shift_logits[:, resp_start:, :]   # [B, Lr, V]
0427 |         resp_labels = shift_labels[:, resp_start:]      # [B, Lr]
0428 |         log.debug("Response portion: logits=%s, labels=%s", 
0429 |                      resp_logits.shape, resp_labels.shape)
0430 | 
0431 |         # Handle empty response case gracefully
0432 |         if resp_labels.numel() == 0:
0433 |             log.warning("Empty response after processing, returning safe defaults")
0434 |             vocab_est = (
0435 |                 getattr(self.tok, "vocab_size", None)
0436 |                 or (len(getattr(self.tok, "get_vocab")() or {}) if hasattr(self.tok, "get_vocab") else None)
0437 |                 or 32000  # Reasonable default for most models
0438 |             )
0439 |             return dict(
0440 |                 mean_logprob=0.0,
0441 |                 ppl=float("inf"),
0442 |                 entropy_mean=math.log(vocab_est),  # Maximum entropy for uniform distribution
0443 |                 len_tokens=0,
0444 |                 len_chars=len(resp),
0445 |                 bytes_len=self._bytes_len(resp),
0446 |                 sum_nll_nats=0.0,
0447 |                 bpb=0.0,
0448 |             )
0449 | 
0450 |         # Compute log probabilities for actual response tokens
0451 |         logprobs = F.log_softmax(resp_logits, dim=-1)              # [B, Lr, V]
0452 |         chosen_lp = torch.gather(logprobs, dim=-1, index=resp_labels.unsqueeze(-1)).squeeze(-1)  # [B, Lr]
0453 |         mean_logprob = float(chosen_lp.mean().item())
0454 |         log.debug("Mean log probability: %.4f", mean_logprob)
0455 | 
0456 |         # Compute token-level entropy (uncertainty measure)
0457 |         probs = logprobs.exp()
0458 |         ent = -(probs * logprobs).sum(dim=-1)                      # [B, Lr]
0459 |         entropy_mean = float(ent.mean().item())
0460 |         log.debug("Mean entropy: %.4f nats", entropy_mean)
0461 | 
0462 |         # Compute perplexity (standard language model metric)
0463 |         ppl = float(math.exp(-mean_logprob))
0464 |         log.debug("Perplexity: %.2f", ppl)
0465 | 
0466 |         # Information-theoretic measures
0467 |         sum_nll_nats = float(-chosen_lp.sum().item())  # Total negative log likelihood
0468 |         bytes_len = self._bytes_len(resp)
0469 |         bpb = self._to_bits(sum_nll_nats) / max(bytes_len, 1)      # Bits per byte
0470 |         log.debug("Information metrics: sum_nll=%.2f nats, bytes=%d, bpb=%.3f", 
0471 |                      sum_nll_nats, bytes_len, bpb)
0472 | 
0473 |         return dict(
0474 |             mean_logprob=mean_logprob,
0475 |             ppl=ppl,
0476 |             entropy_mean=entropy_mean,
0477 |             len_tokens=int(resp_labels.numel()),
0478 |             len_chars=len(resp),
0479 |             bytes_len=int(bytes_len),
0480 |             sum_nll_nats=sum_nll_nats,
0481 |             bpb=float(bpb),
0482 |         )
0483 | 
0484 |     # -----------------------------
0485 |     # Feature Vector Construction
0486 |     # -----------------------------
0487 | 
0488 |     def _build_base_vector(self, alias: str, attrs: Dict[str, Any]) -> Dict[str, Any]:
0489 |         """
0490 |         Build standardized feature vector from computed attributes.
0491 |         
0492 |         Creates a consistent vector representation that can be used by:
0493 |         - Machine learning models for downstream tasks
0494 |         - Plugin systems for enhanced scoring
0495 |         - Monitoring and analysis systems
0496 |         
0497 |         The vector uses namespaced keys to avoid collisions when multiple
0498 |         models or scorers are used in the same system.
0499 | 
0500 |         Args:
0501 |             alias: Model alias for namespacing (e.g., "hf", "gpt", "llama")
0502 |             attrs: Dictionary of computed attributes from _ll_stats
0503 |             
0504 |         Returns:
0505 |             Dictionary containing:
0506 |             - vector: Dict of feature names to values
0507 |             - columns: List of feature names in consistent order
0508 |             - values: List of feature values matching columns order
0509 |         """
0510 |         log.debug("Building base vector for alias: %s", alias)
0511 |         
0512 |         # Define feature keys with namespacing
0513 |         keys = [
0514 |             f"{alias}.mean_logprob",    # Average log probability
0515 |             f"{alias}.ppl",             # Perplexity
0516 |             f"{alias}.entropy_mean",    # Average entropy
0517 |             f"{alias}.len_tokens",      # Token length
0518 |             f"{alias}.len_chars",       # Character length
0519 |             f"{alias}.bytes_len",       # Byte length

0546 |     def _bytes_len(self, s: str) -> int:
0547 |         """
0548 |         Safely compute UTF-8 byte length of a string.
0549 |         
0550 |         Args:
0551 |             s: Input string to measure
0552 |             
0553 |         Returns:
0554 |             Number of bytes when encoded as UTF-8, or character length as fallback
0555 |         """
0556 |         try:
0557 |             return len(s.encode("utf-8"))
0558 |         except Exception as e:
0559 |             log.debug("UTF-8 encoding failed, using character length: %s", str(e))
0560 |             return len(s)
0561 | 
0562 |     def _to_bits(self, nats: float) -> float:
0563 |         """
0564 |         Convert nats to bits for information-theoretic measures.
0565 |         
0566 |         Args:
0567 |             nats: Value in nats (natural log units)
0568 |             
0569 |         Returns:
0570 |             Value in bits (log2 units)
0571 |             
0572 |         Note:
0573 |             Conversion formula: bits = nats / ln(2)
0574 |         """
0575 |         return float(nats / math.log(2.0))
0576 | 
0577 |     # -----------------------------
0578 |     # Resource Cleanup
0579 |     # -----------------------------
0580 | 
0581 |     def close(self):
0582 |         """
0583 |         Comprehensive resource cleanup and memory management.
0584 |         
0585 |         This method ensures proper cleanup of HuggingFace models and tokenizers
0586 |         to prevent memory leaks and resource contention. It handles:
0587 |         - Accelerate hook removal
0588 |         - Model offloading and reference clearing
0589 |         - Tokenizer cleanup
0590 |         - GPU memory cleanup and cache clearing
0591 |         - Parent class cleanup chain
0592 |         
0593 |         Should be called when the scorer is no longer needed to free resources.
0594 |         """
0595 |         log.info("Closing HuggingFaceScorer and cleaning up resources")
0596 |         try:
0597 |             # 0) Remove accelerate hooks if present to prevent reference cycles
0598 |             try:
0599 |                 import accelerate
0600 |                 accelerate.hooks.remove_hook_from_submodules(self.model)
0601 |                 log.debug("Removed accelerate hooks")
0602 |             except Exception as e:
0603 |                 log.debug("No accelerate hooks to remove: %s", str(e))
0604 | 
0605 |             # 1) Move model to CPU and drop references for GC
0606 |             if getattr(self, "model", None) is not None:
0607 |                 try:
0608 |                     # Clear device mapping to break cross-device references
0609 |                     if hasattr(self.model, "hf_device_map"):
0610 |                         self.model.hf_device_map = None
0611 |                     # Move to CPU before deletion
0612 |                     self.model.to("cpu")
0613 |                     log.debug("Moved model to CPU")
0614 |                 except Exception as e:
0615 |                     log.warning("Error moving model to CPU: %s", str(e))
0616 |                 finally:
0617 |                     self.model = None
0618 |                     log.debug("Cleared model reference")
0619 | 
0620 |             # 2) Drop tokenizer reference
0621 |             if getattr(self, "tok", None) is not None:
0622 |                 self.tok = None
0623 |                 log.debug("Cleared tokenizer reference")
0624 | 
0625 |             # 3) Teardown any offload managers
0626 |             try:
0627 |                 offload = getattr(self, "_cpu_offload", None)
0628 |                 if offload and hasattr(offload, "teardown"):
0629 |                     offload.teardown()
0630 |                     log.debug("Tore down CPU offload manager")
0631 |             except Exception as e:
0632 |                 log.debug("No CPU offload manager to teardown: %s", str(e))
0633 | 
0634 |             # 4) Aggressive garbage collection and memory cleanup
0635 |             gc.collect()
0636 |             if torch.cuda.is_available():
0637 |                 torch.cuda.synchronize()
0638 |                 torch.cuda.empty_cache()
0639 |                 torch.cuda.ipc_collect()
0640 |                 torch.cuda.reset_peak_memory_stats()
0641 |                 log.debug("Cleaned GPU memory and cache")
0642 |                 
0643 |         except Exception as e:
0644 |             log.error("Error during HuggingFaceScorer cleanup: %s", str(e))
0645 |         finally:
0646 |             # Always call parent cleanup for plugin teardown
0647 |             super().close()
0648 |             log.info("HuggingFaceScorer closed successfully")
```

```python
0323 | def _build_scm_from_hrm(

0325 | ) -> Dict[str, float]:
0326 |     """Dimension-specific SCM mapping for HRM using internal signals only."""
0327 | 
0328 |     def _clip01(x: float) -> float:
0329 |         try:
0330 |             return float(min(1.0, max(0.0, x)))
0331 |         except Exception:

0333 |

0349 |

0370 |         cons = 0.5
```

```python
0115 |         goal_text = context.get(GOAL, {}).get("goal_text") or ""
0116 |         candidate = getattr(scorable, "text", "") or ""
0117 | 
0118 |         if not goal_text or not candidate:
0119 |             neutral = 0.5
0120 |             res = ScoreResult(
0121 |                 dimension="knowledge",
0122 |                 score=neutral,
0123 |                 source="knowledge",
0124 |                 rationale="missing_goal_or_text",
0125 |                 weight=1.0,
0126 |                 attributes={"normalized_score": neutral, "aux_used": self.aux_features},
0127 |             )
0128 |             return ScoreBundle(results={"knowledge": res})
0129 | 
0130 |         meta = self._aux_from_context(context, scorable)
0131 | 
0132 |         # One model call gives you the blended prob + attribution
0133 |         p, comps = self.model.predict(
0134 |             goal_text,
0135 |             candidate,
0136 |             meta=meta,
0137 |             return_components=True,
0138 |         )

0140 |         # Optional post-calibration (only if your tuner is prob-calibrated)

0146 |         p = max(lo, min(hi, float(p)))

0156 |                     text=getattr(scorable, "text", ""),

0158 |                         "agent_name": "knowledge_scorer",
0159 |                         "section_name": getattr(scorable, "section_name", None),
0160 |                         "paper_id": getattr(scorable, "paper_id", None),
0161 |                         "human_logit": comps["human_logit"],
0162 |                         "ai_logit": comps["ai_logit"],
0163 |                         "sigmoid_gap": head_gap,
0164 |                     },
0165 |                 )
0166 |             except Exception:
0167 |                 pass
0168 | 
0169 |         # Build result (pass through the model’s diagnostics)

0171 |             "probability": round(p, 4),
0172 |             "human_prob": round(comps["human_prob"], 4),

0175 |             "ai_logit": round(comps["ai_logit"], 4),
0176 |             "head_gap": round(head_gap, 4),

0179 |             "human_component": round(comps["human_component"], 4),
0180 |             "ai_component": round(comps["ai_component"], 4),

0182 |             "ai_fraction": round(comps["ai_fraction"], 4),
0183 |             "aux_used": list(self.aux_features),
0184 |         }
0185 | 
0186 |         res = ScoreResult(
0187 |             dimension="knowledge",
0188 |             score=round(p, 4),
0189 |             source="knowledge",
0190 |             rationale=f"blended_prob={round(p, 4)}",
0191 |             weight=1.0,
```

```python
0001 | # stephanie/scoring/llm_scorer.py
0002 | from __future__ import annotations
0003 | 
0004 | import re
0005 | from string import Template
0006 | 
0007 | from stephanie.data.score_bundle import ScoreBundle
0008 | from stephanie.data.score_result import ScoreResult
0009 | from stephanie.scoring.scorable import Scorable
0010 | from stephanie.scoring.scorer.base_scorer import BaseScorer
0011 | 
0012 | 
0013 | class LLMScorer(BaseScorer):
0014 |     """
0015 |     Scores a hypothesis using an LLM per dimension.
0016 |     Uses structured templates and flexible response parsers.
0017 |     """
0018 | 
0019 |     def __init__(self, cfg, memory, container, logger, prompt_loader=None, llm_fn=None):
0020 |         super().__init__(cfg, memory, container, logger)
0021 |         self.model_type = "llm"
0022 |         self.prompt_loader = prompt_loader
0023 |         self.llm_fn = llm_fn
0024 |         self.force_rescore = cfg.get("force_rescore", False)    
0025 | 
0026 |     @property
0027 |     def name(self) -> str:
0028 |         return "llm"
0029 | 
0030 |     def _score_core(self, context:dict, scorable: Scorable, dimensions: list[dict], llm_fn=None) -> ScoreBundle:
0031 |         """
0032 |         Scores a Scorable across multiple dimensions using an LLM.
0033 |         Returns a ScoreBundle object.
0034 |         Accepts either:
0035 |         - A list of dimension names (strings)
0036 |         - A list of dimension dicts: {name, prompt_template, weight, parser, etc.}
0037 |         """
0038 |         results = []
0039 | 
0040 |         for dim in dimensions:
0041 |             prompt = self._render_prompt(context, scorable, dim)
0042 |             prompt_hash = hash(prompt)
0043 | 
0044 |             if not self.force_rescore:
0045 |                 cached_result = self.memory.scores.get_score_by_prompt_hash(prompt_hash)
0046 |                 if cached_result:
0047 |                     self.logger.log("ScoreCacheHit", {"dimension": dim["name"]})
0048 |                     result = cached_result
0049 |                     results.append(result)
0050 |                     continue
0051 | 
0052 |             if not llm_fn:
0053 |                 llm_fn = self.llm_fn
0054 |             response = llm_fn(prompt, context)
0055 | 
0056 |             try:
0057 |                 parser = dim.get("parser") or self._get_parser(dim)
0058 |                 score = parser(response)
0059 |             except Exception as e:
0060 |                 score = 0.0
0061 |                 if self.logger:
0062 |                     self.logger.log(
0063 |                         "LLMScoreParseError",
0064 |                         {
0065 |                             "dimension": dim["name"],
0066 |                             "response": response,
0067 |                             "error": str(e),
0068 |                         },
0069 |                     )
0070 | 
0071 |             if self.logger:
0072 |                 self.logger.log(
0073 |                     "LLMJudgeScorerDimension",
0074 |                     {
0075 |                         "dimension": dim["name"],
0076 |                         "score": score,
0077 |                         "rationale": response,
0078 |                     },
0079 |                 )
0080 | 
0081 |             result = ScoreResult(
0082 |                 dimension=dim["name"],
0083 |                 score=score,
0084 |                 rationale=response,
0085 |                 weight=dim.get("weight", 1.0),
0086 |                 source="llm",
0087 |             )
0088 | 
0089 |             results.append(result)
0090 | 
0091 |         # Aggregate scores across dimensions
0092 |         bundle = ScoreBundle(results={r.dimension: r for r in results})
0093 |         self.memory.evaluations.save_bundle(
0094 |             bundle=bundle,
0095 |             scorable=scorable,
0096 |             context=context,
0097 |             cfg=self.cfg,
0098 |             agent_name=self.name,
0099 |             source=self.scorer.model_type,
0100 |             model_name=self.scorer.get_model_name(),
0101 |             evaluator=self.scorer.name,
0102 |         )
0103 |         return bundle
0104 | 
0105 | 
0106 |     def _render_prompt(self, context: dict, scorable: Scorable, dim: dict) -> str:
0107 |         merged_context = {
0108 |             "scorable": scorable,
0109 |             **context
0110 |         }
0111 |         if self.prompt_loader and dim.get("file"):
0112 |             return self.prompt_loader.score_prompt(
0113 |                 file_name=dim["file"], config=self.cfg, context=merged_context
0114 |             )
0115 |         else:
0116 |             return Template(dim["prompt_template"]).substitute(merged_context)
0117 | 
0118 |     def _default_prompt(self, dimension):
0119 |         return (
0120 |             "Evaluate the following document based on $dimension:\n\n"
0121 |             "Goal: $goal\nHypothesis: $scorable\n\n"
0122 |             "Respond with a score and rationale."
0123 |         ).replace("$dimension", dimension)
0124 | 
0125 |     def _aggregate(self, results: dict) -> float:
0126 |         total = 0.0
0127 |         weight_sum = 0.0
0128 |         for dim, val in results.items():
0129 |             if not isinstance(val, dict):
0130 |                 continue
0131 |             total += val["score"] * val.get("weight", 1.0)
0132 |             weight_sum += val.get("weight", 1.0)
0133 |         return round(total / weight_sum, 2) if weight_sum else 0.0
0134 | 
0135 |     @staticmethod
0136 |     def extract_score_from_last_line(response: str) -> float:
0137 |         lines = response.strip().splitlines()
0138 |         for line in reversed(lines):
0139 |             match = re.search(
0140 |                 r"score[:\-]?\s*(\d+(\.\d+)?)", line.strip(), re.IGNORECASE
0141 |             )
0142 |             if match:
0143 |                 return float(match.group(1))
0144 |         return 0.0
0145 | 
0146 |     @staticmethod
0147 |     def parse_numeric_cor(response: str) -> float:
0148 |         match = re.search(
0149 |             r"<answer>\s*\[\[(\d+(?:\.\d+)?)\]\]\s*</answer>", response, re.IGNORECASE
0150 |         )
0151 |         if not match:
0152 |             raise ValueError(
0153 |                 f"Could not extract numeric score from CoR-style answer: {response}"
0154 |             )
0155 |         return float(match.group(1))
0156 | 
0157 |     def _get_parser(self, dim: dict):
0158 |         parser_type = dim.get("parser", "numeric")
0159 |         if parser_type == "numeric":
0160 |             return self.extract_score_from_last_line
0161 |         if parser_type == "numeric_cor":
0162 |             return self.parse_numeric_cor
0163 |         return lambda r: 0.0
```

```python
0001 | # stephanie/scoring/meta_review_scorer.py
0002 | from __future__ import annotations
0003 | 
0004 | from stephanie.scoring.scorer.base_scorer import BaseScorer
0005 | from stephanie.scoring.scorer.llm_scorer import LLMScorer
0006 | from stephanie.scoring.scorer.mrq_scorer import \
0007 |     MRQScorer  # formerly MRQEvaluator
0008 | 
0009 | 
0010 | class MetaReviewScorer(BaseScorer):
0011 |     """
0012 |     Combines MR.Q-based scoring with LLM fallback.
0013 | 
0014 |     Tries MRQ first. If it's missing dimensions or returns low-confidence scores, falls back to LLM.
0015 |     """
0016 | 
0017 |     def __init__(self, cfg, memory, logger, container, fallback_to_llm=True):
0018 |         super().__init__(cfg, memory, container, logger)
0019 |         self.memory = memory
0020 |         self.logger = logger
0021 |         self.cfg = cfg or {}
0022 |         self.use_llm_fallback = fallback_to_llm
0023 | 
0024 |         self.mrq_scorer = MRQScorer(cfg, memory, container, logger)
0025 |         self.llm_scorer = LLMScorer(cfg, memory, container, logger)
0026 | 
0027 |     def _score_core(self, goal, hypothesis, dimensions):
0028 |         mrq_scores = self.mrq_scorer.score(goal, hypothesis, dimensions)
0029 | 
0030 |         if self._needs_llm_fallback(mrq_scores, dimensions):
0031 |             self.logger.log(
0032 |                 "MetaReviewFallbackTriggered",
0033 |                 {"reason": "Missing or low-confidence MRQ scores", "fallback": "llm"},
0034 |             )
0035 |             llm_scores = self.llm_scorer.score(goal, hypothesis, dimensions)
0036 |             return self._combine_scores(mrq_scores, llm_scores)
0037 |         else:
0038 |             return mrq_scores
0039 | 
0040 |     def _needs_llm_fallback(self, scores, dimensions):
0041 |         """
0042 |         Trigger fallback if:
0043 |         - Any dimension is missing in MRQ
0044 |         - Any score is None or clearly untrained (e.g., 0.0)
0045 |         """
0046 |         for dim in dimensions:
0047 |             if dim not in scores:
0048 |                 return True
0049 |             if abs(scores[dim]["score"] - 0.0) < 1e-8:
0050 |                 return True
0051 |         return False
0052 | 
0053 |     def _combine_scores(self, mrq_scores, llm_scores):
0054 |         """
0055 |         Merge: prefer MRQ if valid, otherwise use LLM.
0056 |         """
0057 |         combined = {}
0058 |         all_dims = set(mrq_scores.keys()) | set(llm_scores.keys())
0059 |         for dim in all_dims:
0060 |             if dim in mrq_scores and mrq_scores[dim]["score"] > 0.0:
0061 |                 combined[dim] = mrq_scores[dim]
0062 |             else:
0063 |                 combined[dim] = llm_scores.get(
0064 |                     dim,
0065 |                     {"score": 0.0, "rationale": "No fallback available", "weight": 1.0},
0066 |                 )
0067 |         return combined
```

```python
0001 | # stephanie/scoring/scorer/model_health.py
0002 | from __future__ import annotations
0003 | 
0004 | import logging
0005 | from dataclasses import dataclass
0006 | from typing import Any, Dict, Optional, Sequence
0007 | 
0008 | from stephanie.utils.hash_utils import hash_dict
0009 |

0012 | 
0013 | @dataclass
0014 | class LoadAudit:
0015 |     missing: Sequence[str]
0016 |     unexpected: Sequence[str]
0017 | 
0018 |     @property
0019 |     def ok(self) -> bool:
0020 |         return (not self.missing) and (not self.unexpected)
0021 | 
0022 | 
0023 | def audit_load_state_dict(
0024 |     model, state_dict: Dict[str, Any], *, strict: bool = False
0025 | ) -> LoadAudit:
0026 |     """
0027 |     Loads state_dict and returns missing/unexpected keys.
0028 |     Always uses strict=False by default, but audits it.
0029 |     """
0030 |     missing, unexpected = model.load_state_dict(state_dict, strict=strict)
0031 |     return LoadAudit(missing=missing, unexpected=unexpected)
0032 | 
0033 | 
0034 | def run_self_test_if_available(
0035 |     model, *, device: str = "cpu", n_trials: int = 8
0036 | ):
0037 |     fn = getattr(model, "self_test", None)
0038 |     if not callable(fn):
0039 |         return None
0040 | 
0041 |     try:
0042 |         out = fn(device=device, n_trials=n_trials)
0043 |         if isinstance(out, dict) and "ok" in out:
0044 |             return out
0045 |         return {"ok": bool(out), "summary": str(out)}
0046 |     except Exception as e:
0047 |         # Important: don't break scorer init; treat as a failed self-test.
0048 |         return {
0049 |             "ok": False,
0050 |             "summary": f"self_test raised: {type(e).__name__}: {e}",
0051 |         }
0052 | 
0053 | def merge_load_audits(audits: list[LoadAudit]) -> Optional[LoadAudit]:
0054 |     """
0055 |     Merge multiple LoadAudit objects into one.
0056 |     Useful when a 'model' is composed of multiple modules with separate state_dicts
0057 |     (e.g., SICQL encoder + q/v/pi heads).
0058 |     """
0059 |     missing: list[str] = []
0060 |     unexpected: list[str] = []
0061 | 
0062 |     any_audit = False
0063 |     for a in audits:
0064 |         if a is None:
0065 |             continue
0066 |         any_audit = True
0067 |         missing.extend(list(a.missing or []))
0068 |         unexpected.extend(list(a.unexpected or []))
0069 | 
0070 |     if not any_audit:
0071 |         return None
0072 | 
0073 |     # NOTE: ok is a @property computed from missing/unexpected
0074 |     return LoadAudit(missing=missing, unexpected=unexpected)
0075 | 
0076 | 
0077 | class ModelHealthLogger:
0078 |     """
0079 |     Centralized logging policy:
0080 |       - error on load missing/unexpected
0081 |       - warning only when self_test ok=False OR load audit not ok
0082 |       - silent on success
0083 |     """
0084 | 
0085 |     def __init__(
0086 |         self,
0087 |         *,
0088 |         enabled: bool = True,
0089 |         self_test_enabled: bool = True,
0090 |         self_test_device: str = "cpu",
0091 |         self_test_trials: int = 8,
0092 |         warn_on_load_issues: bool = True,
0093 |         warn_on_selftest_fail: bool = True,
0094 |     ) -> None:
0095 |         self.enabled = enabled
0096 |         self.self_test_enabled = self_test_enabled
0097 |         self.self_test_device = self_test_device
0098 |         self.self_test_trials = self_test_trials
0099 |         self.warn_on_load_issues = warn_on_load_issues
0100 |         self.warn_on_selftest_fail = warn_on_selftest_fail
0101 | 
0102 |         # Optional: prevent repeated logs per scorer instance
0103 |         self._seen: set[tuple[str, str]] = set()  # (scorer_name, dimension)
0104 |         self._warned_once: set[str] = set()
0105 | 
0106 |     def check_and_log(
```

```python
0002 | """

0033 | from stephanie.utils.file_utils import load_json

0035 | 
0036 | 
0037 | class MRQScorer(BaseScorer):
0038 |     """
0039 |     Multi-dimensional Response Quality Scorer
0040 |     
0041 |     Computes pairwise quality scores for (goal, response) pairs using encoder-predictor models.
0042 |     For each dimension, produces a logit that is scaled to the dimension's target range using
0043 |     either a RegressionTuner (calibrated probability mapping) or sigmoid with linear scaling.
0044 |     
0045 |     Features:
0046 |     - Supports multiple quality dimensions (e.g., relevance, coherence, fluency)
0047 |     - Handles model loading and versioning
0048 |     - Provides score normalization and legacy scale conversion

0050 |     """
0051 | 
0052 |     def __init__(self, cfg, memory, container, logger):
0053 |         """Initialize MRQ scorer with configuration and dependencies"""
0054 |         super().__init__(cfg, memory, container, logger)
0055 |         self.model_type = "mrq"

0058 |         self.hdim = memory.embedding.hdim  # Hidden dimension for model
0059 | 
0060 |         # Configuration parameters
0061 |         self.target_type = cfg.get("target_type", "document")
0062 |         self.model_path = cfg.get("model_path", "models")
0063 |         self.version = cfg.get("model_version", "v1")
0064 | 
0065 |         # Model and calibration storage
0066 |         self.models: Dict[str, MRQModel] = {}  # Dimension -> model mapping
0067 |         self.model_meta: Dict[str, dict] = {}  # Model metadata (min/max values)
0068 |         self.tuners: Dict[str, RegressionTuner] = {}  # Calibration tuners
0069 | 
0070 |         # Dimensions to score
0071 |         self.dimensions: List[str] = cfg.get("dimensions", [])
0072 |         self._load_models(self.dimensions)
0073 | 
0074 |     # ---------- model loading and management ----------
0075 | 
0076 |     def _locator(self, dim: str) -> ModelLocator:
0077 |         """Create model locator for specific dimension"""
0078 |         return ModelLocator(
0079 |             root_dir=self.model_path,
0080 |             embedding_type=self.embedding_type,
0081 |             model_type=self.model_type,
0082 |             target_type=self.target_type,
0083 |             dimension=dim,
0084 |             version=self.version,
0085 |         )
0086 | 
0087 |     def _load_models(self, dimensions: List[str]) -> None:
0088 |         """Load models and calibration tuners for all dimensions"""
0089 |         for dim in dimensions:
0090 |             loc = self._locator(dim)
0091 | 
0092 |             # Build model architecture matching the training setup
0093 |             encoder = TextEncoder(dim=self.dim, hdim=self.hdim).to(self.device)
0094 |             predictor = ValuePredictor(zsa_dim=self.dim, hdim=self.hdim).to(self.device)
0095 | 
0096 |             # Load trained weights
0097 |             encoder.load_state_dict(torch.load(loc.encoder_file(), map_location=self.device))
0098 |             predictor.load_state_dict(torch.load(loc.model_file(), map_location=self.device))
0099 | 
0100 |             # Create complete MRQ model
0101 |             model = MRQModel(
0102 |                 encoder=encoder,
0103 |                 predictor=predictor,
0104 |                 embedding_store=self.memory.embedding,
0105 |                 device=self.device,
0106 |             )
0107 |             self.models[dim] = model
0108 | 
0109 |             # Load model metadata and calibration tuner if available
0110 |             meta = load_json(loc.meta_file()) if os.path.exists(loc.meta_file()) else {"min_value": 0.0, "max_value": 100.0}
0111 |             self.model_meta[dim] = meta
0112 | 
0113 |             tuner_path = loc.tuner_file()
0114 |             if os.path.exists(tuner_path):
0115 |                 t = RegressionTuner(dimension=dim)
0116 |                 t.load(tuner_path)
0117 |                 self.tuners[dim] = t
0118 | 
0119 |     # ---------- score scaling and normalization ----------
0120 | 
0121 |     def _scale(self, dim: str, logit: float, meta: dict) -> float:
0122 |         """
0123 |         Convert raw model logit to normalized score in [0, 1] range
0124 |         
0125 |         Process:
0126 |         1. Apply sigmoid to get probability (0-1)
0127 |         2. Use RegressionTuner if available, else linear scaling with meta min/max
0128 |         3. Detect and handle legacy 0-100 scales, converting to 0-1
0129 |         4. Clamp final result to valid [0, 1] range
0130 |         
0131 |         Args:
0132 |             dim: Dimension name for tuner lookup
0133 |             logit: Raw model output
0134 |             meta: Model metadata with min/max values
0135 |             
0136 |         Returns:
0137 |             Normalized score in [0, 1] range
0138 |         """
0139 |         # Convert logit to probability using sigmoid
0140 |         prob = torch.sigmoid(torch.tensor(logit, dtype=torch.float32)).item()
0141 | 
0142 |         # Apply scaling: use tuner if available, else linear scaling
0143 |         if dim in self.tuners:
0144 |             val_raw = float(self.tuners[dim].transform(prob))
0145 |             min_v = float(meta.get("min_value", 0.0))
0146 |             max_v = float(meta.get("max_value", 1.0))
0147 |         else:
0148 |             min_v = float(meta.get("min_value", 0.0))
0149 |             max_v = float(meta.get("max_value", 1.0))
0150 |             val_raw = prob * (max_v - min_v) + min_v
0151 | 
0152 |         # Handle legacy 0-100 scale models by detecting values > 1.01
0153 |         if max_v > 1.01 or val_raw > 1.01:
0154 |             # Convert from 0-100 scale to 0-1
0155 |             span = (max_v - min_v) if (max_v - min_v) > 0 else 100.0
0156 |             val01 = (val_raw - min_v) / span
0157 |         else:
0158 |             # Already in 0-1 scale
0159 |             span = (max_v - min_v) if (max_v - min_v) > 0 else 1.0
0160 |             val01 = (val_raw - min_v) / span
0161 | 
0162 |         # Ensure score is within valid range
0163 |         return max(0.0, min(1.0, val01))
0164 | 
0165 |     def _score_core(self, context: dict, scorable, dimensions: List[Union[str, dict]]) -> ScoreBundle:
0166 |         """
0167 |         Score a response against goal text across specified dimensions
0168 |         
0169 |         Process:
0170 |         1. Extract goal and response texts
0171 |         2. Compute embeddings for both texts
0172 |         3. For each dimension, run model inference
0173 |         4. Scale raw outputs to normalized scores
0174 |         5. Return comprehensive score bundle
0175 |         
0176 |         Args:
0177 |             context: Contains goal information
0178 |             scorable: Response to be scored
0179 |             dimensions: List of dimension names or configs to score against
0180 |             
0181 |         Returns:
0182 |             ScoreBundle with results for all dimensions
0183 |         """
0184 |         # Extract texts for scoring
0185 |         goal = context.get(GOAL, {})
0186 |         goal_text = goal.get(GOAL_TEXT, "") or ""
0187 | 
0188 |         # Compute embeddings once for efficiency
0189 |         g_np = self.memory.embedding.get_or_create(goal_text)
0190 |         o_np = self.memory.embedding.get_or_create(scorable.text)
0191 |         g = torch.tensor(g_np, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)
0192 |         o = torch.tensor(o_np, dtype=torch.float32, device=self.device).unsqueeze(0)
0193 | 
0194 |         results: Dict[str, ScoreResult] = {}
0195 | 
0196 |         # Score across all specified dimensions
0197 |         for dim in dimensions:
0198 |             dim_name = dim.get("name") if isinstance(dim, dict) else dim
0199 |             model = self.models.get(dim_name)
0200 |             if model is None:
0201 |                 continue
0202 | 
0203 |             # Model inference
0204 |             with torch.no_grad():
0205 |                 z = model.encoder(g, o)  # Encode text pair
0206 |                 logit = float(model.predictor(z).view(-1)[0].item())  # Raw prediction
0207 |                 prob = float(torch.sigmoid(torch.tensor(logit)).item())  # Probability
0208 | 
0209 |             # Scale to normalized score
0210 |             meta = self.model_meta.get(dim_name, {"min_value": 0.0, "max_value": 1.0})
0211 |             score01 = self._scale(dim_name, logit, meta)  # Final 0-1 score
0212 | 
0213 |             # Build result with comprehensive attributes
0214 |             attributes = {
0215 |                 "q_value": round(logit, 6),  # Raw logit
0216 |                 "prob": round(prob, 6),      # Sigmoid probability  
0217 |                 "energy": logit,              # Alternative name for logit
0218 |                 "min_value": 0.0,            # Normalized range
0219 |                 "max_value": 1.0,            # Normalized range
0220 |             }
0221 | 
0222 |             results[dim_name] = ScoreResult(
0223 |                 dimension=dim_name,
0224 |                 score=round(score01, 4),     # Final normalized score
0225 |                 source=self.model_type,
0226 |                 rationale=f"logit={logit:.4f}, prob={prob:.4f}",  # Debug info
0227 |                 weight=1.0,
0228 |                 attributes=attributes,
0229 |             )
0230 | 
0231 |         return ScoreBundle(results=results)
```

```python
0001 | # stephanie/scoring/proximity_scorer.py
0002 | from __future__ import annotations
0003 | 
0004 | import numpy as np
0005 | from scipy.spatial.distance import cityblock, cosine, euclidean
0006 | from sklearn.feature_extraction.text import TfidfVectorizer
0007 | 
0008 | from stephanie.data.score_bundle import ScoreBundle
0009 | from stephanie.data.score_result import ScoreResult
0010 | from stephanie.utils import compute_similarity_matrix
0011 | 
0012 | 
0013 | def jaccard_similarity(a: str, b: str) -> float:
0014 |     set_a, set_b = set(a.lower().split()), set(b.lower().split())
0015 |     return len(set_a & set_b) / len(set_a | set_b) if set_a | set_b else 0.0
0016 | 
0017 | def tfidf_cosine(a: str, b: str) -> float:
0018 |     vec = TfidfVectorizer().fit([a, b])
0019 |     mat = vec.transform([a, b]).toarray()
0020 |     return 1 - cosine(mat[0], mat[1])
0021 | 
0022 | def cosine_similarity(v1, v2) -> float:
0023 |     return 1 - cosine(v1, v2)
0024 | 
0025 | def euclidean_similarity(v1, v2) -> float:
0026 |     return 1 / (1 + euclidean(v1, v2))
0027 | 
0028 | def manhattan_similarity(v1, v2) -> float:
0029 |     return 1 / (1 + cityblock(v1, v2))
0030 | 
0031 | 
0032 | # Registry of all available metrics
0033 | METRIC_REGISTRY = {
0034 |     "jaccard": lambda a, b, *_: jaccard_similarity(a, b),
0035 |     "tfidf": lambda a, b, *_: tfidf_cosine(a, b),
0036 |     "cosine": lambda _, __, v1, v2: cosine_similarity(v1, v2),
0037 |     "euclidean": lambda _, __, v1, v2: euclidean_similarity(v1, v2),
0038 |     "manhattan": lambda _, __, v1, v2: manhattan_similarity(v1, v2),
0039 | }
0040 | 
0041 | class ProximityScorer:
0042 |     """
0043 |     Proximity-based scorer for hypotheses.
0044 |     Uses multiple similarity/distance metrics as dimensions.
0045 |     """
0046 | 
0047 |     def __init__(self, cfg, memory, container, logger):
0048 |         self.cfg = cfg
0049 |         self.memory = memory
0050 |         self.logger = logger
0051 |         self.similarity_threshold = cfg.get("similarity_threshold", 0.75)
0052 |         self.max_pairs = cfg.get("max_graft_candidates", 5)
0053 |         self.top_k_db = cfg.get("top_k_database_matches", 10)
0054 |         self.use_db = cfg.get("use_database_search", True)
0055 |         self.model_type = "proximity"
0056 | 
0057 |     def _score_core(self, context: dict, scorable, metrics: list[dict] = {}) -> ScoreBundle:
0058 |         """
0059 |         Compute proximity-based scores for a given scorable in context.
0060 | 
0061 |         Args:
0062 |             context (dict): Pipeline or agent context containing "hypotheses".
0063 |             scorable: The scorable object (must have .text).
0064 |             metrics (list[dict]): Metric definitions from config.
0065 | 
0066 |         Returns:
0067 |             ScoreBundle: Containing one ScoreResult per proximity metric.
0068 |         """
0069 |         text = scorable.text
0070 | 
0071 |         # Step 1. Collect hypotheses
0072 |         hypotheses = []
0073 |         if context and "hypotheses" in context:
0074 |             hypotheses = [h["text"] for h in context["hypotheses"]]
0075 |         if text and text not in hypotheses:
0076 |             hypotheses.append(text)
0077 | 
0078 |         if not hypotheses:
0079 |             empty_result = ScoreResult(
0080 |                 dimension="avg_similarity",
0081 |                 score=0.0,
0082 |                 source=self.model_type,
0083 |                 rationale="No hypotheses to compare.",
0084 |                 weight=1.0,
0085 |                 attributes={"pair_count": 0},
0086 |             )
0087 |             return ScoreBundle(results={"avg_similarity": empty_result})
0088 | 
0089 |         # Step 2. Compute similarity matrix
0090 |         similarities = compute_similarity_matrix(hypotheses, self.memory, self.logger)
0091 | 
0092 |         # Step 3. Compute metrics
0093 |         metrics = self._compute_metrics(similarities, hypotheses, text)
0094 | 
0095 |         # Step 4. Wrap metrics as ScoreResults
0096 |         results = {}
0097 |         for dim, meta in metrics.items():
0098 |             results[dim] = ScoreResult(
0099 |                 dimension=dim,

0101 |                 source=self.model_type,
0102 |                 rationale=meta["rationale"],
0103 |                 weight=meta["weight"],
0104 |                 attributes=meta.get("attributes", {}),
0105 |             )

0109 |     def _compute_metrics(self, similarities, hypotheses, target_text):

0123 | 
0124 |         # Core stats
0125 |         avg_sim = float(np.mean(sims))
0126 |         max_sim = float(np.max(sims))
0127 |         min_sim = float(np.min(sims))
0128 |         sim_var = float(np.var(sims))
0129 |         sims_sorted = sorted(sims, reverse=True)[: self.max_pairs]
0130 |         avg_topk = float(np.mean(sims_sorted)) if sims_sorted else 0.0
0131 | 
0132 |         graft_pairs = [(h1, h2) for h1, h2, s in similarities if s >= self.similarity_threshold]
0133 |         graft_count = len(graft_pairs)

0135 |         # Cluster measures
0136 |         cluster_density = graft_count / pair_count if pair_count > 0 else 0.0
0137 |         redundancy_index = avg_topk  # high top-k mean → redundancy
0138 |         novelty_index = 1.0 - min_sim  # inverse of worst similarity
0139 | 
0140 |         # DB measures (optional)
```
